and as associations of attachment (*saṃprayoga-bandhana*) toward the sense-bases of mind (*manāyatana*) and mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*) that are associated with them.
The afflictions associated with auditory consciousness act as objects of attachment toward the sense-base of sound (*śabdāyatana*).
In relation to those associated [factors], there is a bond of association with the sense-base of mind (*manāyatana*) and the sense-base of mental objects (*dharmāyatana*).
As for the afflictions associated with olfactory consciousness, there is a bond of objective condition (*ālambanabandhana*) with respect to the sense-base of odors (*gandhāyatana*),
and a bond of association with respect to those associated [factors] within the sense-base of mind and the sense-base of mental objects.
The afflictions associated with tongue-consciousness function as objects of attachment (*ālambana-bandhana*) toward the sphere of taste (*rasāyatana*);
they function as associations (*saṃprayoga-bandhana*) toward the sphere of mind (*manāyatana*) and the sphere of mental phenomena (*dharmāyatana*) that are associated with them.
The afflictions associated with body-consciousness form a bond through the object-condition (*ālambana-pratyaya*) upon the sphere of tangibles (*spraṣṭavyāyatana*).

They form a bond through the association-condition (*samprayoga-pratyaya*) upon the associated spheres of mind (*manāyatana*) and mental objects (*dharmāyatana*). The afflictions associated with mental consciousness (*manovijñāna*) form a bond through the object-condition upon all twelve spheres.
In those cases, there is a connection through association within the sphere of mind (*manāyatana*) and the sphere of mental objects (*dharmāyatana*).
This is called the brief *vibhāṣā* on the single category.
If there is a bond of the fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) regarding this object, is there also a bond of the fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If one is bound by the fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) regarding a certain object, one is necessarily bound by the fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*).
However, there may be cases where one is bound by the fetter of craving but not by the fetter of aversion;
that is, when the fetter of craving for phenomena belonging to the form and formless realms (*rūpa-dhātu* and *ārūpya-dhātu*) has not yet been abandoned.
Among these, the fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) pertains to all three realms and all five categories;
it has only outflowing objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*) and is not universal (*asarvatraga*).
The fetter of hostility (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) pertains only to the desire realm and all five categories.
Only those with outflows (sāsrava) are not universal (asarvatraga).
For those bound by all fetters (sakalabandhana), regarding the five categories of objects in the desire realm (kāmadhātu),
if there is bondage by the fetter of attachment (anunaya-saṃyojana), there is also bondage by the fetter of aversion (pratigha-saṃyojana).
If there is bondage by the fetter of aversion, there is also bondage by the fetter of craving regarding the five categories of things in the realms of form and formlessness; however,
there is bondage by the fetter of craving but not by the fetter of aversion [regarding those same objects].
For one who is not yet free from bondage, regarding the five categories of objects in the desire realm,
there is a bond of the fetter of craving (anunaya-saṃyojana) wherever it has not been abandoned,
and there is also a bond of the fetter of aversion (pratigha-saṃyojana).
If, in that which has already been abandoned, there is neither the fetter of craving nor the fetter of aversion,
regarding the five categories of things in the realms of form and formlessness.
Wherever it has not been abandoned, there is the fetter of craving;
there is no fetter of ill-will.
Where it has already been abandoned, there is no fetter of craving.
Nor is there a bond of ill-will (pratigha-saṃyojana),
because the bond of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) is long while the bond of ill-will is short.
To the question asked, one should provide an answer according to the subsequent clause (paścāt-pādaka).
If there is a bond of aversion (pratigha-saṃyojana) regarding this object, there must necessarily be a bond of craving (anunaya-saṃyojana).
That is to say, regarding objects within the five categories of the desire realm that have not yet been completely abandoned,
there may be a bond of craving.
There is no bondage by the fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*).
This refers to the fact that the fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) has not been abandoned with respect to phenomena of the form and formless realms.
Within this, there may be eight stages (*bhūmi*) that have not yet been abandoned.
Up to and including the case where the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception has not been abandoned;
within this stage, there may be some of the five categories that have not been abandoned,
up to and including the case where those to be abandoned by cultivation have not been abandoned.
Within this category, there may be nine grades that have not yet been abandoned,
up to and including the lowest-of-the-low grade that has not yet been abandoned;
here, the term "not yet abandoned" is stated in its general sense.
Question: For what reason are the five categories of dharmas in the form and formless realms not bound by the fetter of ill-will (*vyāpāda-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: Because the two upper realms lack the fetter of ill-will.
Question: For what reason do the two upper realms lack the fetter of ill-will?
The answer is: because they are not a fit vessel for the fetter of ill-will (*vyāpāda-saṃyojana*).
Furthermore, all practitioners of yoga (*yogācāra*) feel weary of the fetter of ill-will and seek the two higher realms;
if those two higher realms possessed the fetter of ill-will, [they would not do so].
Yogācāras should not seek that which involves diligent application of effort.
If a phenomenon exists in a lower stage and also exists in a higher stage,
then there would be no gradual cessation of phenomena.
If this did not exist, there would likewise be no such thing as the ultimate cessation of phenomena,
for that [cessation] is what is brought about by it.
Furthermore, if one were to deny the existence of ultimate cessation, one would likewise have to deny liberation and transcendence.
To avoid such an error, there is no fetter of malice (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) in the two higher realms.
Furthermore, the fetter of malice necessarily depends upon a coarse and harsh continuum;
because the continua of the form and formless realms are subtle and smooth, being nourished by superior *śamatha*, they lack the fetter of malice.
Furthermore, if within this realm there are the faculties of grief and suffering, then there is the fetter of malice (*pratigha-saṃyojana*).
This is because sentient beings, relying on the faculties of grief and suffering, give rise to hatred toward the mental continuums of others.
Because the realms of form and formlessness lack the faculties of grief and suffering, there is no fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*).
Furthermore, if there is a lack of shame (*āhrīkya*) and a lack of dread of blame (*anapatrāpya*) within the desire realm, then the fetter of ill-will exists;
for sentient beings, relying upon a lack of shame and a lack of dread of blame, give rise to hatred toward the mental continuums of others.
Because the two upper realms lack shame (*āhrīkya*) and lack of dread (*anapatrāpya*), they lack the fetter of ill-will (*vyāpāda-saṃyojana*).
Furthermore, if envy (*īrṣyā*) and avarice (*mātsarya*) exist in a realm, there is the fetter of ill-will;
for sentient beings, relying upon envy and avarice, give rise to hatred toward the mental continuums of others.
In the form and formless realms, because envy (*īrṣyā*) and avarice (*mātsarya*) are absent, there is no fetter of ill-will (*vyāpādasaṃyojana*).
Furthermore, if within a realm there are female and male faculties (*strīpuruṣendriya*), then the fetter of ill-will exists;
for sentient beings, depending upon these female and male faculties, give rise to hatred toward the mental continuums of others.
Because the female and male faculties are absent in the form and formless realms, there is no fetter of ill-will (*vyāpāda-saṃyojana*).
Furthermore, if there were craving for edible food (*kavaḍīkāra-āhāra*) in these realms, there would be the fetter of ill-will;
for sentient beings, depending on craving for edible food, give rise to hatred toward the mental continuums of others.
Because there is no craving for edible food in the form and formless realms, the fetter of ill-will (*vyāpāda-saṃyojana*) does not exist there.
Furthermore, if there is craving for sexual desire in these realms, then the fetter of ill-will exists;
this is because sentient beings, depending on craving for sexual desire, give rise to hatred toward the mental continuums of others.
In the form and formless realms, because there is no craving for sensual desire, there is no fetter of ill will (*vyāpāda-saṃyojana*).
Furthermore, if the five hindrances (*nīvaraṇa*) exist in these realms, then the fetter of ill will exists as well;
for sentient beings, depending upon the five hindrances, give rise to malice toward the mental continuums of others.
Because the realms of form and formlessness lack the fivefold hindrances (*nīvaraṇa*), there is no fetter of ill-will (*vyāpāda-saṃyojana*).
Furthermore, if within a realm there are the five objects of sensual pleasure (*pañca kāmaguṇāḥ*), then the fetter of ill-will exists;
for sentient beings give rise to hatred and anger based upon these five objects of sensual pleasure.
Because the realms of form and formlessness lack the five exquisite sensual desires, there is no fetter of ill will (*vyāpāda-saṃyojana*).
Furthermore, if within these realms there is the characteristic of enmity and aversion, then the fetter of ill will exists.
As for the characteristic of enmity and aversion:
This refers to the nine bases of malice (*āghāta-vastu*).
Because there is no characteristic of enmity or aversion in the form and formless realms, the fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) does not exist there.
For this reason, the Venerable Ghoṣaka stated:
When sentient beings encounter signs of enmity or aversion, they give rise to the fetter of hatred (*pratigha-saṃyojana*).
Since such signs of enmity and aversion do not exist in the two upper realms, the fetter of hatred is absent there.
Furthermore, loving-kindness (*maitrī*) is the proximate path that serves as the direct antidote to the fetter of hatred.
Because the realm of form (rūpadhātu) possesses loving-kindness (maitrī),
it is free from the fetter of ill-will (vyāpāda-saṃyojana). It is like a place where,
if the Vairambha wind blows, clouds and smoke cannot possibly remain.
Since the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) does not exist [for them], the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*) likewise does not exist.
This is because afflictions (*kleśa*) that do not exist in a lower stage cannot be gradually abandoned in a higher stage.
If there is a bond of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) regarding a particular object, is there also a bond of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*) regarding that same object?
Answer: It is so.
If there is the bond of conceit (māna-saṃyojana), is there also the bond of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana)?
Answer: It is so.
That is to say, the fetters of craving (*tṛṣṇā*) and pride (*māna*) pertain to all three realms and all five categories (*pañca-varga*).
They are exclusively associated with outflowing objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*) and are not universal (*asarvatraga*), due to differences such as their duration and so forth.
The question should be answered by constructing a statement in this manner.
If one is fully bound,
all objects belonging to the five categories within the three realms are bound by two fetters;
for one who is not fully bound, it is otherwise.
In the stage that has already been abandoned, there is no connection with the two fetters;
in the stage not yet abandoned, there is connection with the two fetters.
This may pertain to nine stages, or even down to a single stage; within these stages, it may consist of five categories, or even down to a single category.
Within this category, there may be nine grades or even as few as one grade;
therefore, it is said "thus.
If, regarding a particular object, there is bondage by the fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*), is there also bondage by the fetter of ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*)?

Answer: If there is bondage by the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) regarding this object, there is necessarily bondage by the fetter of ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*); or there may be bondage by the fetter of ignorance without bondage by the fetter of craving.
This refers to the case when the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has already arisen, but the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen.
Regarding those dharmas abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*),
there remains the fetter of ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*) to be abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*) which has not yet been severed;
herein, the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) pervades all three realms and all five categories (*pañca-nikāya*).
Only those with outflows (sāsrava) have objects that are not universal (asarvatraga).
The fetter of ignorance (avidyā-saṃyojana) extends across the three realms and all five categories (pañca-varga),
taking as its objects both those with outflows and those without outflows (anāsrava), and being both universal and non-universal.
For those who are bound by all fetters regarding the five categories of phenomena within the three realms,
if they are bound by the fetter of craving, they are also bound by the fetter of ignorance;
if they are bound by the fetter of ignorance, they are also bound by the fetter of craving.
In one who is not yet free from the fetters, regarding that which has already been abandoned,
there may be the binding of the pervasive ignorance-fetter and the binding of the craving-fetter;
therein, the ignorance-fetter is predominant.

Because the fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) is brief, the answer to the question should be formulated according to the preceding clause: that is to say, regarding the objects belonging to the five categories within the three realms, wherever there is the binding of the fetter of craving, there must also be the binding of the fetter of ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*).
There may be those who are bound by the fetter of ignorance but not bound by the fetter of craving;
this is explained in detail as before:
that is, when the knowledge of suffering has already arisen, but the knowledge of the origin has not yet arisen.
The fetters of craving and ignorance abandoned through the vision of suffering have already been completely severed with respect to their own category of objects; therefore,
neither of them can bind.

The pervasive ignorance-fetter (avidyā-saṃyojana) to be abandoned by the vision of the origin (samudaya-darśana-prahātavya) is bound to its object (ālambana-bandhana) regarding the entities to be abandoned by the vision of suffering (duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya).
The craving-fetter (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) to be abandoned by the vision of the origin is likewise [bound] regarding the entities to be abandoned by the vision of suffering.
It is not bound by the object-condition because it is not a universal [mental factor].
It is not bound by association because it belongs to a different category.
If one is bound by the fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) regarding a certain object, is one also bound by the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*)?
One should respond that this involves four permutations (*catuṣkoṭika*).
Herein, the fetter of craving pertains to all three realms and all five categories (*pañca nikāyāḥ*).
Only those with outflows (*sāsrava*) are not universal (*asarvatraga*).

The fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) extends across the three realms and comprises all four categories; it takes both objects with and without outflows as its conditions, and includes both universal and non-universal [factors].
For those bound by all fetters (*sakalabandhana*), this pertains to the five categories of phenomena within the three realms.
If one is bound by the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*), one is also bound by the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*);
if one is bound by the fetter of views, one is also bound by the fetter of craving.
For those who are not fully bound, the fetter of craving is more extensive because it pervades all five categories (*pañca-varga*).
Only those with outflows as their object are short because they are not universal;
the fetter of views is short because it consists of only four categories.
That which takes both objects with and without outflows, and is both universal and non-universal, is long. Thus, these two possess the sense of being mutually long and short.
The question should be answered by means of a fourfold formulation (*catuṣkoṭi*).
There may be one who is bound by the fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) but not bound by the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*;
this refers to one for whom the knowledge of origination has arisen, but the knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen).
Regarding those factors dissociated from the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) which are to be abandoned by the vision of cessation and the path,
as well as those factors to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*) for which the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) has not yet been abandoned—
among these, "factors dissociated from the fetter of views to be abandoned by the vision of cessation and the path" refers to...

This refers to the collection of phenomena associated with or dissociated from that wrong view— namely, its own nature as well as views, grasping at views, grasping at precepts and observances, doubt, greed, hatred, pride, and unshared ignorance—
and because craving for these various phenomena has not been abandoned.
One who is bound by the fetter of craving is bound toward their own group both by way of the object-condition and by way of association;
if they are bound toward another's group, it is only by way of the object-condition.
There is no bondage by the fetter of views that is not associated with the bondage [of other defilements]. Why is this?
Because those universal fetters of views that take the five categories as their object have already been abandoned.
As for the remaining [defilements] that have not yet been abandoned, they are not bound to these factors dissociated from the fetter of views by way of being an object,
because they take the untainted as their object.
It is not bound by association,
because it belongs to a different category;
for a self-nature does not associate with itself.
Because they have not yet abandoned craving for the factors to be abandoned by cultivation, they are bound by the fetter of craving; that is,
there may be those who have not yet abandoned the fetter of craving in nine stages,
or even those who have not yet abandoned it in a single stage.

Within this stage, there may be nine grades of the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) that have not yet been abandoned, up to and including the case where even a single grade of the fetter of craving has not yet been abandoned, yet there is no binding by the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*). Why is this? Because those universal fetters of views that take the five categories as their objects have already been abandoned.
Because the category of factors abandoned by cultivation lacks the fetter of views.
Furthermore, when the knowledge of cessation has arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen,
[the practitioner is] dissociated from the factors abandoned by the path of seeing that are associated with the fetter of views.
And regarding the factors to be abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*),
there is the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) that has not yet been abandoned.
Among these, the factors dissociated from the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) which are to be abandoned by the path of seeing (*darśana-mārga*) are as previously explained.
Regarding these phenomena and those phenomena to be abandoned through cultivation,
there is bondage by the fetter of craving and no bondage by the fetter of views, as previously explained.
Furthermore, for a disciple of the Blessed One who possesses right view, the fetter of craving toward phenomena to be abandoned through cultivation remains unabandoned.

In this context, because the knowledge of the path (mārga-anvaya-jñāna) has already arisen and one has thus fully seen the four noble truths of the three realms, one is said to be "one who has seen" (dṛṣṭi-prāpta).
Nevertheless, because that person has not yet abandoned craving for the phenomena to be abandoned through cultivation (bhāvanā-heya), [they are not yet an arhat].
There may be one who is bound by the fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*)— either with the fetter of craving of nine stages (*bhūmi*) not yet abandoned,

or even with that of a single stage not yet abandoned— and within those stages, there may be the fetter of craving of nine grades (*prakāra*) not yet abandoned, or even that of a single grade not yet abandoned, while being without the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*).
Why is this? Because all fetters of views have been severed by him.
There may be cases where one is bound by the fetter of views but not bound by the fetter of craving.
This refers to the case where the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has already arisen, but the knowledge of origination (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen;
thus, regarding the phenomena to be abandoned by the vision of suffering, the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) to be abandoned by the vision of origination remains unsevered.
In this context, the knowledge of suffering has arisen while the knowledge of origination has not yet arisen.
The fetter of craving and the fetter of views, both of which are to be abandoned by the vision of suffering, have already been abandoned;
however, because the fetter of views to be abandoned by the vision of the origin [of suffering] has not yet been abandoned,
it constitutes a bond as an object-condition (*ālambana-bandhana*) with respect to those phenomena to be abandoned by the vision of suffering.

Although the fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) to be abandoned by seeing the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*) has not yet been severed, it does not constitute a connection as an object (*ālambana-bandhana*) with respect to phenomena to be abandoned by seeing suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*),
because it is not universal (*asarvatraga*); nor does it constitute a connection through association (*saṃprayoga-bandhana*).
Because it belongs to that category [of defilements],
there may be cases where both are bound;
that is to say, for one who is fully fettered (*sakalabandhana*), there are two types of fetters (*saṃyojana*) regarding the phenomena to be abandoned through seeing and cultivation.
Question: For what reason is one called "bound by all fetters" (*sakalabandhana*)?
Answer: Because this sentient being is able to bind all constituent parts, and because all constituent parts are bound.
This is called "possessing all fetters.
Regarding the statement that "all members are capable of binding," it means that the afflictions of all five categories are capable of acting as fetters.
"One whose all constituent parts are bound" means that the dharmas of the five classes are all bound.

This one who is fully bound possesses the bond of the fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) for one class of the dharmas to be abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), and the bond of the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) for two classes.
The same applies to the phenomena abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*).
Regarding the phenomena associated with the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*),
there is bondage by one portion of the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) and bondage by the three portions of the fetter of views.

Regarding factors dissociated from the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*), there is bondage by one portion of the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) and bondage by three portions of the fetter of views.
It is the same for factors to be abandoned by the path of seeing (*darśana-mārga-prahātavya*).
Regarding factors to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-mārga-prahātavya*), there is bondage by one portion of the fetter of craving and bondage by two portions of the fetter of views.
Furthermore, when the knowledge of suffering has arisen but the knowledge of the origin has not yet arisen,
there are two fetters binding one to the phenomena abandoned through the vision of the origin, as well as those abandoned through the cultivation of the cessation and the path.
Among these, regarding the phenomena abandoned through the vision of the origin:
There is one portion bound by the fetter of craving and one portion bound by the fetter of views.
Regarding those phenomena associated with the fetter of views that are to be abandoned through the vision of cessation,
there is one portion bound by the fetter of craving and two portions bound by the fetter of views.
Regarding phenomena dissociated from the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*),
there is bondage by one portion of the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) and bondage by one portion of the fetter of views.
The same applies to phenomena to be abandoned by the path of vision (*darśana-mārga-prahātavya*).

Regarding the factors to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*), there is bondage by the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) for one portion and bondage by the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) for another portion.
At that time, although there is bondage by the fetter of views regarding the factors to be abandoned by seeing suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-heya*), there is no bondage by the fetter of craving.
Therefore, this is not mentioned.
Furthermore, when the knowledge of origination (*samudaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-jñāna*) has not yet arisen,
there are two fetters (*saṃyojana*) binding those factors associated with the views to be abandoned by the vision of cessation and the path (*darśana-nirodha-mārga-prahātavya*).
In this context, regarding those phenomena associated with the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) that are to be abandoned by the vision of cessation and the path,
there is a binding by one portion of the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) and a binding by one portion of the fetter of views.

At that time, regarding those phenomena dissociated from the fetter of views that are to be abandoned by the vision of cessation and the path, as well as those phenomena to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).
Although there is the fetter of craving (rāga-saṃyojana), there is no fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana);
therefore, this is not mentioned.
Furthermore, when the knowledge of cessation (nirodha-jñāna) has already arisen but the knowledge of the path (mārga-jñāna) has not yet arisen.
Regarding the factors associated with the fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana) to be abandoned by the path of seeing, there are two types of fettering.
Among these, for the factors associated with the fetter of views to be abandoned by the path of seeing,
there is the fettering of one portion of the fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) and the fettering of one portion of the fetter of views.

At that time, regarding those factors dissociated from the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) which are abandoned through the path of seeing, as well as those factors abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*),
although there is the binding of the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*), there is no binding of the fetter of views.
Therefore, this is not mentioned.
Alternatively, there may be cases where both are unconditioned (aniyata),
namely when the knowledge of origin (samudaya-jñāna) has already arisen but the knowledge of cessation (nirodha-jñāna) has not yet arisen.

Regarding the phenomena abandoned through the vision of suffering and its origin, there is no bondage by two fetters when the knowledge of cessation has already arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen.
Regarding the phenomena abandoned through the vision of suffering, its origin, and its cessation, there is no bondage by two fetters [in that same state].
A disciple of the World-Honored One who possesses right view has no fetters of the two types bound to phenomena abandoned by seeing;
one who is already free from the defilement of desire has no fetters of the two types bound to phenomena of the desire realm;
and one who is already free from the defilement of form has no fetters of the two types bound to phenomena of the desire and form realms.
Having already abandoned the defilements of the formless realm, one is no longer bound by the two fetters regarding the phenomena of the three realms;
because both the fettering factors and the fettered objects therein have been severed, one is entirely free from these two fetters.
This means that they are both dissociated from the fetters of craving and views.
Furthermore, one should formulate the following question and answer:
Is there any phenomenon associated with the fetter of views that is abandoned through the vision of cessation or the vision of the path?

Is there a case where one is bound by the fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) but not bound by the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*), and yet is not subject to the increase of the underlying tendency (*anuśaya*) of non-viewing?
Answer: There is.
This refers to one who, having abandoned the six grades of fetters, has entered the state of rightness and departure from birth (*samyaktva-niyāma*).
In this state, the knowledge of origination (*samudaya-jñāna*) has already arisen, but the knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-jñāna*) has not yet arisen.

Regarding the phenomena associated with the six preceding grades of fetters of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) that are to be abandoned by the vision of cessation and the path, there is the bondage of the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*).
Regarding the latter three grades [of the desire realm], because the fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) has not yet been abandoned with respect to them;
regarding the universal fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*), because that which takes all five categories as its object has already been abandoned;
and because the fetter of views taking the uncontaminated (*anāsrava*) as its object—which belongs to one's own category and consists of the first six grades—has also already been abandoned.

Although the fetters of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) directed toward the outflow-free (*anāsrava*) objects within the latter three categories of one's own school have not yet been abandoned, they do not constitute an object-fetter (*ālambana-bandhana*) with respect to the factors associated with the views already abandoned in the former six categories; because [those views] are directed toward the outflow-free, they do not constitute an association-fetter (*samprayoga-bandhana*).
Because they belong to a different category (*nikāya*),
the latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) of [wrong] view do not fail to increase [with respect to them].

This is because the [latent dispositions of] view-grasping (*dṛṣṭiparāmarśa*) and adherence to precepts and observances (*śīlavrataparāmarśa*) still increase with respect to the last three categories of their own class even when compared to the first six categories.
The latent tendencies of views (dṛṣṭyanuśaya) encompass all five views,
whereas the fetter of views (dṛṣṭisaṃyojana) consists only of the first three views;
this is as in the case of the fetter of views.
The same applies to the fetter of doubt (*vicikitsā-saṃyojana*).
That is to say, just as the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) pertains to all three realms, consists of only four categories,
and encompasses both contaminated and uncontaminated objects, as well as universal and non-universal [defilements].
The fetter of doubt is likewise.
Therefore, regarding the fetter of craving, it is as if it were facing the fetter of views.
If there is a binding by the fetter of craving with respect to a certain object, is there also a binding by the fetter of grasping?
It is agreed that these shall be explained in four propositions (*catuṣkoṭi*).

Among them, the fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) pertains to all three realms and all five categories (*pañca-varga*), is exclusively associated with the outflowing (*sāsrava*) objects, and is not universal (*asarvatraga*).
The fetter of grasping (*parāmarśa-saṃyojana*) pertains to all three realms and consists of only four categories, and is associated with the outflowing objects.
Regarding both pervasive and non-pervasive universal factors:
for those bound by all fetters, with respect to the objects of the five categories within the three realms,
if there is a bond of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*), there is also a bond of grasping (*parigraha-saṃyojana*).

If there is one bound by the fetter of grasping (*upādāna-saṃyojana*), there is also one bound by the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) who is not fully bound. Because the fetter of craving extends across all five categories (*pañca-varga*), it is "long";
because it is exclusively non-universal (*asarvatraga*), it is "short. The fetter of grasping extends across both universal and non-universal [categories], and is therefore "long."
Because there are only four categories, [the text] is brief.
Since these two possess the sense of being mutually long or short, the question should be answered by means of a fourfold alternative (catuṣkoṭika).
There may be one who is bound by the fetter of craving (anunaya-saṃyojana) but not bound by the fetter of grasping (parāmarśa-saṃyojana).

That is to say: when the knowledge of origination has arisen but the knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen, there is an unabandoned fetter of craving toward phenomena to be abandoned through cultivation;
or when the knowledge of cessation has arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen.
Regarding the phenomena to be abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*), there is the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) that has not yet been abandoned.
A disciple of the Blessed One who possesses right view may also have this fetter of craving for phenomena to be abandoned through cultivation not yet abandoned;
in this case, there may be the fetter of craving for the nine stages that has not yet been abandoned.
Furthermore, there may be a case where the fetter of craving for a certain stage has not yet been abandoned;
within that stage, there may be nine grades of the fetter of craving that have not been abandoned, or even as few as one grade of the fetter of craving that has not been abandoned.
Because they have not been abandoned, there is the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) and the fetter of grasping (*upādāna-saṃyojana*). Why is this?
Because the universal fetter of grasping that takes the five categories as its object has already been abandoned.
The pervasive fetter of grasping (*parāmarśa-saṃyojana*) has not been abandoned;
for once it is abandoned, it can no longer act as a bond with respect to phenomena to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*),
since the category of phenomena to be abandoned by cultivation lacks the fetter of grasping.
There may be one who is bound by the fetter of grasping (*upādāna-saṃyojana*) but not bound by the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*).
This refers to a case where the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has already arisen, but the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen;

thus, regarding the phenomena to be abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-heya*), the fetter of grasping to be abandoned through the vision of origin (*samudaya-darśana-heya*) has not yet been severed.
In this case, although the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has already arisen, the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen.
Both the fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) and the fetter of grasping (*parigraha-saṃyojana*) abandoned through the vision of suffering have already been severed;
however, because the fetter of grasping abandoned through the vision of origin has not yet been severed.
Regarding the phenomena abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), they constitute objects of bondage (*ālambana-bandhana*).

Although the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) abandoned through the vision of origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*) has not yet been severed, it does not constitute an object of bondage for the phenomena abandoned through the vision of suffering,
because it is not a universal [defilement] (*asarvatraga*).
Because that which is bound by non-associated [fetters] belongs to another category.
Alternatively, there may be those bound by both;
that is, one who is fully fettered has the bonds of the two types of fetters regarding phenomena abandoned through seeing and cultivation.

In this context, one who is bound by all fetters is bound to the phenomena abandoned through the vision of suffering by one category of the fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) and two categories of the fetter of grasping (*parāmarśa-saṃyojana*);
it is the same for the phenomena abandoned through the vision of the origin [of suffering].
Regarding the phenomena to be abandoned by the vision of cessation,
there is the fetter of craving (anunaya-saṃyojana) binding one category and the fetter of grasping (parāmarśa-saṃyojana) binding three categories;
it is the same for the phenomena to be abandoned by the vision of the path.
Regarding the dharmas to be abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*),
there is a portion bound by the fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) and two portions bound by the fetter of grasping (*parāmarśa-saṃyojana*).
Furthermore, when the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen.
Regarding the phenomena abandoned through the cultivation of the truths of origin, cessation, and the path, there are two fetters that bind them. Among these,
regarding the phenomena abandoned through the vision of origin,
there is the binding of the fetter of craving (anunaya-saṃyojana) and the binding of the fetter of grasping (parāmarśa-saṃyojana), each belonging to one category.
Regarding the phenomena abandoned through the vision of cessation and the path,
there is, for each, a single category of the fetter of craving and two categories of the fetter of grasping;
regarding the phenomena abandoned through cultivation:
There is a case where one is bound by the fetter of craving for one category and bound by the fetter of grasping for another category;
at that time, although there is binding by the fetter of grasping regarding phenomena to be abandoned through the vision of suffering, there is no binding by the fetter of craving.
Therefore, this is not mentioned.
Furthermore, when the knowledge of origination has arisen but the knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen,
there are two fetters binding one to the phenomena abandoned through the vision of the cessation and the path.
In this context, regarding the phenomena abandoned through the vision of the cessation and the path,
there is a bond of the fetter of craving (anunaya-saṃyojana) for one portion and a bond of the fetter of grasping (parāmarśa-saṃyojana) for one portion;
at that time, regarding the phenomena abandoned through cultivation (bhāvanā-heya).
Although there is the fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*), there is no fetter of grasping (*parāmarśa-saṃyojana*);
therefore, this is not mentioned.
Furthermore, when the knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-jñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of the path (*mārga-jñāna*) has not yet arisen.
Regarding the phenomena abandoned through the path of seeing, there are two fetters that bind them:
herein, regarding the phenomena abandoned through the path of seeing,
there is the binding of the fetter of craving belonging to one category and the binding of the fetter of grasping belonging to one category.

At that time, although there is the bondage of the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) regarding the factors to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*), there is no bondage of the fetter of grasping (*upādāna-saṃyojana*);
therefore, this is not mentioned.
Alternatively, there may be cases where neither of the two is present.

That is to say: when the knowledge of origination (*samudaya-jñāna*) has arisen but the knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-jñāna*) has not yet arisen, there is no bondage by the two fetters (*saṃyojana*) regarding those phenomena to be abandoned through the vision of suffering and origination;
and when the knowledge of cessation has arisen but the knowledge of the path (*mārga-jñāna*) has not yet arisen.
Regarding the phenomena to be abandoned through the vision of suffering, origin, and cessation, there are no two fetters that bind them.
A disciple of the Blessed One who possesses vision has no two fetters binding him regarding the phenomena to be abandoned through vision.
Having already abandoned the defilement of desire, one is not bound by the two fetters regarding the phenomena of the desire realm.
Having already abandoned the defilement of form, one is not bound by the two fetters regarding the phenomena of the desire and form realms.
Having already abandoned the defilement of the formless, one is not bound by the two fetters regarding the phenomena of the three realms.
In this context, because all phenomena—both the fetters and the fettered—are already abandoned, they are all free from the two bonds;
that is to say, they are dissociated from both the bond of craving (*tṛṣṇā*) and the bond of grasping (*upādāna*).
If there is the bond of the fetter of craving with respect to a given thing, is there also the bond of the fetter of envy (*īrṣyā*)?
Answer: If there is a bond of envy (*īrṣyā-saṃyojana*) regarding a particular object, there must necessarily be a bond of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*).
However, there may be a bond of craving without a bond of envy;

that is to say, when the bond of craving has not yet been abandoned with respect to dharmas to be abandoned by insight (*darśana-heya*) in the desire realm, as well as with respect to dharmas in the form and formless realms.
Among these, the fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) pertains to all three realms and all five categories;
it has only outflowing objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*) and is not universal (*asarvatraga*).
The fetter of envy (*īrṣyā-saṃyojana*) belongs only to the desire realm, is abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*), has outflowing objects, and is not universal.
For those who are bound by all fetters, regarding matters to be abandoned through cultivation in the desire realm:
if there is the bond of the fetter of craving, there is also the bond of the fetter of envy;
if there is the bond of the fetter of envy, there is also the bond of the fetter of craving.
Regarding the objects of the four categories abandoned through seeing in the desire realm, as well as the objects of the five categories in the form and formless realms,
there is bondage by the fetter of craving but no bondage by the fetter of envy.
For one who is not fully bound— if they have not yet abandoned the defilements of desire— there is bondage by both fetters regarding the objects abandoned through cultivation in the desire realm.
Regarding the four categories of objects to be abandoned by insight within the three realms:
wherever they have not yet been abandoned, there is the fetter of craving but not the fetter of envy;
wherever they have already been abandoned, there is neither of the two fetters.
Regarding matters to be abandoned through cultivation in the form and formless realms,
there is bondage by the fetter of craving,
but no bondage by the fetter of envy.
One who has already become free from the defilement of desire is bound by two fetters regarding the five categories of objects in the realm of desire;
regarding the five categories of objects in the realms of form and formlessness,
they are bound by the fetter of craving wherever it has not yet been abandoned, but are not bound by the fetter of envy.
If there is no binding by two fetters at the point where [a fetter] has already been abandoned—
because the fetter of craving is long while the fetter of envy is short—
the answer to the question should be given by means of a subsequent-phrase response (*paścātpādaka*).
If there is a bond of envy (*īrṣyā-saṃyojana*) regarding a given object, there must necessarily be a bond of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*).
This refers to objects in the desire realm that are to be abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*) and from which one has not yet attained dissociation (*visaṃyoga*).
Alternatively, there may be a bond of craving regarding an object without a bond of envy.
This refers to the fact that regarding the phenomena of the desire realm to be abandoned by insight (*darśana-prahātavya*), the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) has not yet been abandoned.
Within this, there may be those for whom four categories of the fetter of craving have not yet been abandoned,
up to and including those for whom even a single category of the fetter of craving has not yet been abandoned.
Regarding the phenomena of the form and formless realms, there is the fetter of craving that has not yet been abandoned;
herein, for some, the fetter of craving for eight stages has not been abandoned,
and so on, up to for others, the fetter of craving for even a single stage has not been abandoned.
Within this stage, there may be five categories of fetters of craving that have not yet been abandoned,
or even as few as one category of fetters of craving that has not yet been abandoned;
within that category, there may be nine grades of fetters of craving that have not yet been abandoned.
Even if there is one category of the fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) that has not yet been abandoned,
because it is not abandoned, there is the bond of the fetter of craving and no bond of the fetter of envy (*īrṣyā-saṃyojana*). Why is this so?
Because the category of factors abandoned through seeing lacks the fetter of envy (*īrṣyā*),
the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*) and the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*) likewise lack the fetter of envy.
They lack both envy and avarice (*mātsarya*), as was previously explained regarding hatred (*vyāpāda*).
As it is with the fetter of envy (*īrṣyā-saṃyojana*),
so it is with the fetter of avarice (*mātsarya-saṃyojana*);
that is to say, both envy and avarice belong exclusively to the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*) and are abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).
Because the outflow-tainted objects are not universal,
just as the fetter of craving forms one category with respect to what follows,
so too does the fetter of pride form one category with respect to what follows.
That is to say, craving (*tṛṣṇā*) and pride (*māna*) both pertain to all three realms and all five categories;

however, because they have only contaminated objects (*sāsravālambana*) and are not universal (*asarvatraga*), if one is bound by the fetter of aversion (*pratighasaṃyojana*) toward a particular object, is one also bound by the fetter of pride toward that same object?
Answer: If one is bound by the fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) regarding a certain object, one is necessarily bound by the fetter of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*).
However, there may be cases where one is bound by the fetter of conceit but not by the fetter of ill-will;
this refers to phenomena belonging to the form and formless realms (*rūpa-dhātu* and *ārūpya-dhātu*).
There is the fetter of pride (*māna-saṃyojana*) that has not yet been abandoned.

Among these, the fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) belongs only to the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*), pertains to all five categories (*pañca-nikāya*), is exclusively with outflow (*sāsrava*) as its object, and is not universal (*apracāra*).
The fetter of pride pertains to all three realms (*tridhātu*) and all five categories.
Only those with outflows as their object are not universal.
For those bound by all fetters, regarding the five categories of objects in the desire realm,
if they are bound by the fetter of ill-will, they are also bound by the fetter of conceit.
If one is bound by the fetter of pride,
one is also bound by the fetter of ill-will regarding the five categories of phenomena in the form and formless realms.
There are those bound by the fetter of pride (māna-saṃyojana) but not by the fetter of ill-will (pratigha-saṃyojana).
For one who is not fully bound, regarding the five categories of objects in the desire realm,
wherever a [particular] category has not yet been abandoned, they are bound both by the fetter of ill-will and by the fetter of pride.

If, regarding the five categories of things in the form and formless realms, there is no bondage by the fetter of ill-will (*vyāpāda-saṃyojana*) where it has already been abandoned, nor any bondage by the fetter of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*),
then according to the points where they have not yet been abandoned, there is bondage by the fetter of conceit and no bondage by the fetter of ill-will.
If, in a state where [the fetter of] pride has already been abandoned, there is neither the binding of the fetter of pride nor the binding of the fetter of ill-will—
because the fetter of ill-will is short while the fetter of pride is long—
the answer to the question should be made by following the "prior clause" (pūrvapada).

If there is a bond of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) regarding a given object, there must necessarily be a bond of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*). This refers to objects within the five categories of the desire realm that have not yet been completely abandoned.
Alternatively, there may be a bond of conceit without a bond of ill-will.
This refers to the dharmas of the form and formless realms;
regarding the fetter of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*) therein, it may be that eight stages have not yet been abandoned,
or even that only one stage has not yet been abandoned.
Within this stage, there may be five categories that have not yet been abandoned,
or even as few as one category that has not yet been abandoned;
within that category, there may be nine grades that have not yet been abandoned.
Even if there remains one category [of defilement] that has not yet been abandoned:
if, regarding a certain object, there is the fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*), is there also the fetter of ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If, regarding a certain object, there is the fetter of ill-will, there must necessarily be the fetter of ignorance.
There may be one who is bound by the fetter of ignorance but not bound by the fetter of ill-will; that is, one who has not yet abandoned the defilement of desire,
for whom the knowledge of suffering has already arisen but the knowledge of origin has not yet arisen,
with respect to those phenomena of the desire realm to be abandoned through the vision of suffering.
There is the fetter of ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*) to be abandoned by the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*) that has not yet been severed.

Among these, the fetter of malice (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) belongs only to the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*), pertains to all five categories (*pañca-varga*), is exclusively with outflow objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*), and is non-pervasive (*apracāra*). The fetter of ignorance, however, pertains to all three realms (*tridhātu*), all five categories, has both outflow and outflow-free objects (*sāsrava-anāsrava-ālambana*), and is both pervasive (*pracāra*) and non-pervasive.
For those who are bound by all fetters regarding the five categories of objects in the desire realm,
if they are bound by the fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*), they are also bound by the fetter of ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*);
and if they are bound by the fetter of ignorance, they are also bound by the fetter of ill-will.
Regarding the five categories of phenomena in the form and formless realms,
there is bondage by the fetter of ignorance and bondage by the fetter of ill-will.
For one who is not fully bound, this applies to those states in the desire realm that have already been abandoned.
There may be those who are bound by the universal fetter of ignorance (avidyā-saṃyojana) but not by the fetter of ill-will (pratigha-saṃyojana);
the same applies to those who have not yet abandoned these in the realms of form and formlessness.
This is because the fetter of ill-will is short-lived, whereas ignorance is long-lasting.
The question should be answered by following the preceding formula:
if one is bound to this object by the fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*), one is necessarily bound by the fetter of ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*).
This refers to objects within the five categories of the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*) that have not yet been abandoned.
There may be one who is bound by the fetter of ignorance but not bound by the fetter of ill-will; that is,
one who has not yet abandoned the defilement of desire, for whom the knowledge of suffering has already arisen but the knowledge of origin has not yet arisen,
with respect to the phenomena of the desire realm to be abandoned through the vision of suffering.
There is the fetter of ignorance to be abandoned by the vision of the origin that has not yet been severed.

In this context, one who has not yet become free from the defilement of desire is so described because, even if they have become free from the defilement of desire, both fetters are absent with respect to the phenomena of the desire realm; therefore, it is said that they have not yet become free from them.
When the knowledge of suffering has arisen but the knowledge of the origin has not yet arisen,
both hatred and ignorance to be abandoned by the vision of suffering have already been abandoned;
however, because the pervasive ignorance to be abandoned by the vision of the origin has not yet been abandoned.
Regarding the factors to be abandoned by the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), there is bondage through being an object (*ālambana-bandhana*).

However, the fetter of malice (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) to be abandoned by the vision of origination (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*) does not bind those factors to be abandoned by the vision of suffering through being an object, because it is not universal (*asarvatraga*).
Because that which is bound by non-associated [factors] belongs to another category.
Furthermore, regarding the factors of the form and formless realms, there exists the fetter of ignorance that has not yet been abandoned;
among these, there may be the fetter of ignorance of the eight stages that has not yet been abandoned.
...up to the point where there may be a certain level (*bhūmi*) whose fetter of ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*) has not yet been abandoned;
within that level, there may be five categories of the fetter of ignorance that have not yet been abandoned,
up to the point where even a single category of the fetter of ignorance has not yet been abandoned.
Within this category, there may be those who have not yet abandoned nine grades of the fetter of ignorance,
up to and including those who have not yet abandoned even a single grade;
because they have not abandoned it, they are bound by the fetter of ignorance.
Because one who is bound by the fetter of ill-will is not bound by that very fetter of ill-will.
If, with respect to a certain object, one is bound by the fetter of ill-will, is one also bound by the fetter of views?
One should answer that this constitutes four permutations (catuṣkoṭi).

Among these, the fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) belongs only to the desire realm, pervades all five categories, has only impure objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*), and is not universal (*asarvatraga*).
The fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) pertains to all three realms,
consists of only four categories, pervades both pure and impure objects, and includes both universal and non-universal [factors].
For those who are bound by all fetters regarding the five categories of objects in the desire realm,
if they are bound by the fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*), they are also bound by the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*);
and if they are bound by the fetter of views, they are also bound by the fetter of ill-will.
Regarding the five categories of phenomena in the form and formless realms,
there is bondage by the fetter of views but no bondage by the fetter of ill-will.
For those who are not fully bound, the fetter of ill-will is longer-lasting because it pervades all five categories.
The fetter of desire (*icchā-saṃyojana*) is short because it pertains only to the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*), has impure objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*), and is not universal (*asarvatraga*).

The fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) is long because it extends across all three realms, has both pure and impure objects (*anāsrava- and sāsrava-ālambana*), and includes both universal and non-universal [factors].
It is short because it consists of only four sections;
since these two possess the sense of being mutually long and short,
the question should be answered by means of a fourfold logical alternative (catuṣkoṭi).
There may be those who are bound by the fetter of aversion but not bound by the fetter of views;
that is to say, one who has not yet abandoned the defilement of desire, for whom the knowledge of origination has already arisen but the knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen,
with respect to those factors of the desire realm associated with the fetter of views that are to be abandoned through the vision of cessation and the vision of the path.
Furthermore, regarding the factors to be abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*) in the desire realm where the fetter of malice (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) has not yet been severed: herein,

those factors associated with the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) that are to be abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana*) and the vision of the path (*mārga-darśana*) refer to the collection of factors—

both associated and dissociated— that consist of the intrinsic nature of false view (*mithyādṛṣṭi*), as well as the grasping at views (*dṛṣṭiparāmarśa*), the grasping at precepts and observances (*śīlavrataparāmarśa*), doubt (*vicikitsā*), greed (*rāga*), hatred (*dveṣa*), pride (*māna*), and non-specific ignorance (*asāmānyāvidyā*).
Because hatred toward these phenomena has not been abandoned, there is the fetter of hatred.
With respect to one's own group, it constitutes both an object-fetter and an association-fetter;
with respect to another's group, it constitutes an object-fetter but not an association-fetter, and there is no fetter of views.
Why is this? Because those universal fetters of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) that take the five categories as their object have already been abandoned.
As for the remaining unabandoned [fetters], they are not bound to these dissociated factors by way of being an object (*ālambana*), because they take uncontaminated (*anāsrava*) objects.
Because that which is bound by association belongs to another category,
and because a self-nature does not associate with itself;
such is the case regarding those factors abandoned through cultivation in the desire realm.
Because hatred has not yet been abandoned, there is the fetter of hatred.
Alternatively, there may be nine grades of the fetter of hatred that have not yet been abandoned,
up to and including the case where even one grade of the fetter of hatred has not yet been abandoned, yet there is no fetter of views.
Why is this? Because those pervasive fetters of views that take the five categories as their object have already been abandoned,
and because the category abandoned through cultivation is devoid of the fetter of views.
Furthermore, when the knowledge of cessation has arisen but the knowledge of the path has not yet arisen,
there is the fetter of views associated with the factors to be abandoned by the vision of the path within the desire realm,
as well as the fetter of ill-will that remains unabandoned regarding the factors to be abandoned by cultivation within the desire realm.
Among these, the factors dissociated from the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) abandoned through the path of seeing are as previously explained.

Regarding these factors and the factors of the desire realm abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*), there is bondage by the fetter of malice (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) but no bondage by the fetter of views, also as previously explained. Furthermore, regarding the disciples of the Blessed One who possess vision (*dṛṣṭi-prāpta*):

For one who has not yet abandoned the defilement of sensual desire, the fetter of ill-will (*vyāpādasaṃyojana*) regarding the factors of the desire realm to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*) remains unsevered.

Because that ill-will regarding the factors of the desire realm to be abandoned by cultivation is unsevered, they are bound by the fetter of ill-will; it should be understood as previously explained that they are not bound by the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭisaṃyojana*).
There may be one who is bound by the fetter of views but not bound by the fetter of ill-will; that is,
one who has not yet abandoned the defilement of desire, for whom the knowledge of suffering has already arisen but the knowledge of origin has not yet arisen,
with respect to those phenomena of the desire realm to be abandoned through the vision of suffering.
There is one for whom the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) to be abandoned by the vision of the origin has not yet been abandoned;
and regarding the phenomena of the form and formless realms, the fetter of views has not yet been abandoned.
In this case, the knowledge of suffering (*duḥkha-jñāna*) has already arisen, but the knowledge of the origin (*samudaya-jñāna*) has not yet arisen.
The fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) and the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*) have both been severed; however,
because the fetter of views abandoned through the vision of origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*) has not yet been severed,
it remains a bond by way of being an object (*ālambana-bandhana*) with respect to those phenomena abandoned through the vision of suffering.
Although the fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) to be abandoned by the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*) has not yet been severed,

it does not constitute a connection as an object (*ālambana-bandhana*) with respect to phenomena to be abandoned by the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), because it is not universal (*asarvatraga*).
Nor does it constitute a connection through association (*saṃprayoga-bandhana*), because it belongs to a different category (*parakīya-nikāya*).
Regarding the phenomena of the form and formless realms,
there are those for whom the fetter of views has not yet been abandoned;
that is, for some, the fetter of views across the eight stages has not yet been abandoned.
...up to the point where there may be a certain level (*bhūmi*) for which the fetters of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) have not yet been abandoned;
within that level, there may be four categories of the fetters of views that have not yet been abandoned,
up to the point where there may be even a single category of the fetters of views that has not yet been abandoned.

Because it has not been abandoned, there is bondage by the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) but no bondage by the fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*), since that [fetter of ill-will] is absent.
Alternatively, there may be bondage by both;

that is to say, for one who is bound by all fetters (*sakalabandhana*), there is bondage by both fetters regarding the dharmas of the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*) that are to be abandoned by vision (*darśana-heya*) and those to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).
For this person bound by all fetters, regarding the factors of the desire realm to be abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*),
there is a bond of the fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) for one category and a bond of the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) for two categories.
It is the same for the factors of the desire realm to be abandoned through the vision of origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*).
Regarding those factors associated with the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) to be abandoned by the vision of cessation within the desire realm:
there is bondage by one category of the fetter of malice (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) and bondage by three categories of the fetter of views.
Regarding those factors dissociated from that fetter of views: [there is no bondage].
There is one category bound by the fetter of aversion and two categories bound by the fetters of views;
the same applies to those factors in the desire realm abandoned through the path of vision.
Regarding the factors in the desire realm abandoned through cultivation: [the same applies].

There is one type of fetter consisting of aversion and two types of fetters consisting of views. Furthermore, for one who has not yet abandoned the defilement of desire, when the knowledge of suffering has arisen but the knowledge of origin has not yet arisen, there are two fetters binding the phenomena of the desire realm that are to be abandoned through the vision of origin, cessation, and the path, as well as through cultivation.
In this context, regarding the phenomena of the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*) abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*),
there is bondage by one portion of the fetter of malice (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) and bondage by one portion of the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*).
Regarding the phenomena associated with the fetter of views that are abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*) in the desire realm:
There is one category bound by the fetter of aversion and two categories bound by the fetters of views;
regarding those factors dissociated from the fetters of views,
there is one category bound by the fetter of aversion and one category bound by the fetters of views.
The same applies to the factors abandoned through the path of seeing (*darśana-mārga*) in the desire realm.
Regarding the factors abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-mārga*) in the desire realm,
there is bondage by one portion of the fetter of malice (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) and bondage by one portion of the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*).
At that time, regarding the dharmas in the desire realm to be abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*),
although there is bondage by the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*), there is no bondage by the fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*); therefore,
this is not mentioned here.
Furthermore, when the knowledge of origination has arisen but the knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen,
there are two fetters binding the phenomena associated with the fetter of views that are to be abandoned through the vision of cessation and the path within the desire realm.

Among these, for one who has not yet abandoned the defilement of desire, there are the phenomena associated with the fetter of views to be abandoned through the vision of cessation and the path within the desire realm.
Each is bound by one portion of the fetter of aversion and one portion of the fetter of views.

At that time, regarding the factors in the desire realm that are dissociated from the fetter of views abandoned through the vision of cessation and the path, as well as those factors abandoned through cultivation:
Although there is the bond of the fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*), because there is no bond of the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*), this is not mentioned.
Furthermore, when the knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-jñāna*) has already arisen but the knowledge of the path (*mārga-jñāna*) has not yet arisen,
there are bonds of two fetters regarding those factors associated with the fetter of views that are to be abandoned by the path of seeing within the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*).

In this context, for one who has not yet abandoned the defilement of desire (*kāmarāga*), regarding those factors associated with the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭisaṃyojana*) to be abandoned by the path of seeing (*darśanamārga*) within the desire realm, there is a connection to one portion of the fetter of aversion (*pratighasaṃyojana*) and a connection to one portion of the fetter of views.

At that time, regarding those factors dissociated from the fetter of views to be abandoned by the path of seeing within the desire realm, as well as those factors to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanāmārga*):
Although there may be the fetter of malice (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) without the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*),
this [case] is not mentioned here. *Abhidharma-jñānaprasthāna-śāstra* and *Mahāvibhāṣā-śāstra*, Fascicle Fifty-six.
The Abhidharma-mahāvibhāṣā-śāstra, Fascicle 57,
composed by five hundred great arhats and others.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Section Two: The Chapter on the Aggregates of Bondage, Part Two of the Second Sub-section on Singlefold Categories. Alternatively, there are those who are bound by neither.
That is to say, when the knowledge of origination has already arisen but the knowledge of cessation has not yet arisen,
with respect to those phenomena abandoned through the vision of suffering and origination,
as well as those phenomena dissociated from the fetter of views abandoned through the vision of cessation and the path within the form and formless realms.
Furthermore, regarding the factors to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*) in the form and formless realms, there are no two fetters (*saṃyojana*) binding them;
this is when the knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-jñāna*) has already arisen, but the knowledge of the path (*mārga-jñāna*) has not yet arisen,
with respect to the factors to be abandoned by seeing suffering, origin, and cessation.
Furthermore, there are no fetters of the two types that bind the factors abandoned through the path of seeing in the form and formless realms,
nor do they bind the factors abandoned through cultivation in the form and formless realms.
A disciple of the World-Honored One who possesses right view,

though not yet free from the defilement of desire, has no two fetters binding them to the states abandoned through vision, nor to those abandoned through cultivation in the realms of form and formlessness.
Having already abandoned the defilement of desire, one is not bound by the two fetters regarding the phenomena of the desire realm.
Having already abandoned the defilement of form, one is not bound by the two fetters regarding the phenomena of the desire and form realms.
Having already abandoned the defilement of the formless, one is not bound by the two fetters regarding the phenomena of the three realms.
In this context, because all phenomena—the fetters and the fettered—have been abandoned, they are all free from the two bonds;
that is, because they are both dissociated from the bond of ill-will (*pratigha*) and the bond of views (*dṛṣṭi*).
Question: Does ill-will exist in the desire realm?
When one attains dissociation from the fetter of ill-will (*vyāpāda-saṃyojana*), one may be said to be "unbound" [from it].
However, since the realms of form and formlessness (*rūpa-dhātu* and *ārūpya-dhātu*) originally lack the fetter of ill-will,
how can it be said that those beings are unbound from the fetter of ill-will?
Answer: There are two kinds of non-bondage: first, becoming non-bound through the severance of bondage;
second, being non-bound by nature.
Therefore, it is called non-bondage.
Because the phenomena of the desire realm possess the fetter of ill-will (*vyāpāda-saṃyojana*),
when liberation is attained, it is said that they pass from being bound to being unbound.
However, the phenomena of the two upper realms are fundamentally devoid of the fetter of ill-will.
Therefore, it is said that they are by nature unbound (*apratisaṃyukta*).
Since the term "unbound" contains two meanings, this is stated as being unbound in both respects.
As the *Vinaya* says, there are two types of persons (*pudgala*).
It is called "purity.
First, one has never transgressed the prohibitive precepts from the very beginning;
second, having transgressed them, one repents and eliminates them in accordance with the Dharma.
First, it is called "pure" because its fundamental nature is undefiled;
second, it is called "pure" because it attains purity from defilement.
The same applies to being unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*).
Therefore, there is no error.
Question: What are the factors dissociated from the fetters of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) that are to be abandoned through the vision of cessation and the path in the form and formless realms?

Answer: They are the factors associated with and dissociated from the collection [of afflictions] consisting of the nature of false view (*mithyādṛṣṭi*), the grasping at views (*dṛṣṭiparāmarśa*), the grasping at precepts and observances (*śīlavrataparāmarśa*), doubt (*vicikitsā*), greed (*rāga*), pride (*māna*), and non-common ignorance (*asāmānyāvidyā*).

Associated phenomena (*saṃprayukta-dharma*) refer to the intrinsic nature of wrong view, the grasping at views (*dṛṣṭi-parāmarśa*), and so forth, up to the collection of unshared ignorance (*āveṇikī-avidyā*), as well as the primary minds (*citta*) and mental factors (*caitta*).
Non-associated phenomena (*viprayukta-dharma*) refer to...
This refers to all four characteristics (lakṣaṇas) within the clusters of wrong view up to the unique ignorance (āveṇikī-avidyā),
as well as the defining characteristics (lakṣaṇas) and the characterized (lakṣya) within the clusters of their respective acquisitions (prāpti),
just as in the case of the fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana).
The same applies to the fetter of doubt (*vicikitsā-saṃyojana*).

That is to say, just as the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) pervades all three realms and consists of only four categories, and pervades both the outflowing (*sāsrava*) and non-outflowing (*anāsrava*), as well as universal (*sarvatraga*) and non-universal objects; so too is the fetter of doubt.
The fetter of doubt is likewise.
Therefore, as with the fetter of hatred in relation to the fetter of views,
if there is the binding of the fetter of hatred toward a particular object, is there also the binding of the fetter of grasping toward that same object?
It should be explained in four propositions.
Among these, the fetter of malice (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) belongs exclusively to the desire realm, pervades all five categories,
is associated only with the outflowing (*sāsrava*) objects, and is not universal (*asarvatraga*).

The fetter of grasping (*upādāna-saṃyojana*) pertains to all three realms and consists of only four categories: those with outflow as objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*), including both universal (*sarvatraga*) and non-universal (*asarvatraga*).
For those who possess all bonds, regarding the five categories of objects in the desire realm, if there is a bond of malice (*pratigha-saṃyojana*), there is also a bond of grasping.
If there is bondage by the fetter of grasping (upādāna-saṃyojana), there is also bondage by the fetter of ill-will (pratigha-saṃyojana).
Regarding the five categories of objects in the form and formless realms,
there is bondage by the fetter of grasping but no bondage by the fetter of ill-will.
In one who is not bound by all fetters (*asamagra-bandhana*), the fetter of malice (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) is short because it belongs only to the desire realm and is not universal (*asarvatraga*);
it is long because it pertains to all five categories (*pañca-nikāya*).
The fetter of grasping (*parāmarśa-saṃyojana*) is short because it pertains only to four categories.
Because they pertain to all three realms and are both universal and non-universal, they are "long.
Since these two possess the sense of being mutually long and short,
the question should be answered by means of a fourfold alternative (catuṣkoṭi).
There may be one who is bound by the fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) but not bound by the fetter of grasping (*parigraha-saṃyojana*).
This refers to one who has not yet abandoned the defilement of desire (*kāmarāga*),
for whom the knowledge of origination (*samudaya-jñāna*) has already arisen, but the knowledge of cessation (*nirodha-jñāna*) has not yet arisen.
Regarding the factors of the desire realm to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*), there is the fetter of ill-will (*vyāpāda-saṃyojana*) that has not yet been abandoned.
Cessation-knowledge (*nirodha-jñāna*) has already arisen, but path-knowledge (*mārga-jñāna*) has not yet arisen.
Regarding the factors of the desire realm to be abandoned by cultivation, there is the fetter of ill-will that has not yet been abandoned.
Among the disciples of the World-Honored One who possess right view,

those who have not yet abandoned the defilement of desire still have the fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) toward the factors of the desire realm to be abandoned through cultivation that remains unsevered;
among these, there may be some for whom the nine grades of the fetter of ill-will remain unsevered.
Furthermore, there may be a case where even a single category of the fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) has not been abandoned.
Because it has not been abandoned, one is bound by the fetter of ill-will and lacks the fetter of grasping (*upādāna-saṃyojana*). Why is this so?
Because the pervasive fetters of grasping (*pariṣvaṅga-agraha-saṃyojana*) that take the five categories as their object have already been abandoned;
for the non-pervasive fetters of grasping cannot bind, whether they are unabandoned or already abandoned, with respect to phenomena to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).
Because the category of factors abandoned by cultivation lacks the fetter of grasping (*upādānasaṃyojana*),
there may be the binding of the fetter of grasping without the binding of the fetter of ill-will (*pratighasaṃyojana*),
namely, in one who has not yet become free from the defilement of desire.
When the knowledge of suffering has arisen but the knowledge of the origin has not yet arisen,
regarding the phenomena of the desire realm to be abandoned by the vision of suffering,
there remains the fetter of grasping to be abandoned by the vision of the origin that has not yet been severed.
Regarding the phenomena of the form and formless realms, the fetters of grasping have not yet been abandoned;
herein, one is not yet free from the defilement of desire,
and while the knowledge of suffering has already arisen, the knowledge of origination has not yet arisen.
