Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree. Section Two: The Chapter on the Aggregates of Fetters (Saṃyojana-skandha), Part Three of the Second Sub-section on Singlefold Categories. If, with respect to this object, there is a past fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) that binds it.
"Are there also those that are future?
and so forth, as explained at length.
Within this context, the various fetters (*saṃyojana*) are of two kinds.
First is delusion regarding specific characteristics;
second is delusion regarding common characteristics.
Delusion regarding specific characteristics refers to the fetters of attachment, aversion, pride, envy, and stinginess.
Delusion regarding common characteristics refers to the fetters of ignorance (*avidyā*), views (*dṛṣṭi*), grasping (*parāmarśa*), and doubt (*vicikitsā*).
Among the fetters that delude one regarding specific characteristics,
the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā*) is able to act as a bond for the objects belonging to the five categories within the three realms.
Regarding future [factors] that are not yet abandoned, they bind all things of the three times.
Regarding past [factors] that are not yet abandoned, it is said that if, with respect to a given thing, [the factor] had previously arisen and was not abandoned, then one is bound;
if it had not previously arisen, or if it had arisen but was subsequently abandoned, then one is not bound.
The present is also indeterminate;
that is to say, regarding this object, if it is present before one, there is bondage;
if it is not present before one, there is no bondage.
The fetter of pride (*māna-saṃyojana*) is likewise.
The fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) can act as a bond with respect to the five categories of objects within the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*).
If it has not been abandoned in the future, it definitely binds all objects of the three times.
The past [factors] are indeterminate.
That is to say, regarding this object, if they arose previously and have not been abandoned, one is bound;
if they did not arise previously, or if they arose but have already been abandoned, one is not bound.
The present is also not fixed;
that is to say, with regard to this object, if it is present before one, one is bound to it;
if it is not present before one, one is not bound to it.
The fetter of envy (*īrṣyā-saṃyojana*) acts as a bond with respect to objects to be abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*) within the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*).
Regarding future [objects] that have not yet been abandoned, it definitely binds all such objects of the three times;
regarding past [objects], it is not fixed.
That is to say, regarding this object, if it arose previously and has not been abandoned, one is bound to it;
if it had not arisen previously, or if having arisen it has been abandoned, one is not bound to it.
Even in the case of the present, it is not fixed.
That is to say, regarding this object, if it is present before one, one is bound;
if it is not present before one, one is not bound.
The fetter of stinginess (*mātsarya-saṃyojana*) is also like this.
The fetters that take the common characteristic as their object can bind the objects belonging to the five categories within the three realms.
Those that are past or future and have not been abandoned definitely bind all such objects throughout the three times.
The present is indeterminate;
that is to say, regarding this matter, if it is present before one, then one is bound;
if it is not present before one, then one is not bound.
This is called the *Saṃkṣipta-vibhāṣā* (Brief Vibhāṣā) concerning the six small and seven large sections. If,
with respect to this object, there is a bond of past craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*),
is there also one of the future?
The answer is: "It is so.
Why is this? Because it was previously stated that the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) can act as a bond with respect to the objects belonging to the five categories within the three realms.
Because future [factors] that have not yet been abandoned are bound to all phenomena of the three times, if there are future [factors], are there also past ones?
Answer: If they were previously produced and have not yet been abandoned, then they are bound.
If it has not previously arisen, or if having arisen it has been abandoned, then one is not bound by it. Why is this?
Because it was stated previously that the past fetter of craving is indeterminate.
That is to say, regarding this object, if it arose previously and has not been abandoned, one is bound to it;
if it had not arisen previously, or if it arose but has already been abandoned, one is not bound to it.
Question: At what time is the past fetter of craving (rāga-saṃyojana) abandoned?
At the very time when the fetter of craving for the future has been severed, it is also severed;
at the very time when the fetter of craving for the past has not been severed,
the fetter of craving for the future has likewise not been severed.
Now, for what reason is it said that if a preceding [defilement] has arisen and not been abandoned, one is bound;
whereas if it has not yet arisen, or if having arisen it has been abandoned, one is not bound?
The masters of foreign lands (bahirdeśaka) explain it in this way:
If those previously arisen have not been severed, one is bound by them;
this refers to the three middle grades of fetters.
If they have not yet arisen, one is not bound by them.
The statement that one is not bound by the lower three grades of fetters once they have arisen and been abandoned refers to the upper three grades of fetters.
The masters of the Kaśmīra country say:
"If one is bound by that which has arisen previously but not yet abandoned,
they speak of nine grades of fetters."
If they have not yet arisen and thus are not bound,
this refers to the latter three categories of fetters (*saṃyojana*).
Furthermore, if they have already arisen but have been abandoned, they are likewise not bound.
Regarding the explanation of the first six categories of fetters (*saṃyojana*):
just as the past six categories of the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) have already been abandoned, so too are they [abandoned] in the future.
This is because, although the last three categories of the fetter of craving have not yet been abandoned, they have not yet arisen.
It is bound by future [fetters], but not by past ones.
The meaning intended here is that if,
regarding this object, the future fetter of craving has not yet been abandoned.
Furthermore, there is the case where the fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) produced in a prior life has not yet been abandoned;
in that case, there is also the sense of being bound by the past fetter of craving with respect to that very object.
Even if the future fetter of craving with respect to that object has not yet been abandoned, [the same applies].
Furthermore, regarding this [object], although the fetter of craving has not yet arisen previously,
even if it arises elsewhere, it is still said in regard to this specific object that it "has not yet arisen.
Even if it were to have arisen and was subsequently abandoned, there would be no sense of being bound by the past fetter of craving in relation to this very object.
If, regarding this object, there is a past fetter of craving (rāga-saṃyojana), is there also a present one?
Answer: If it is present before one. Why is that?
It was stated previously that the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) is also not necessarily present;
that is to say, one is bound to an object only when it is present before one,
but is not bound when it is not present.
That is to say, if the fetter of craving arises with respect to this object and is present,
then there is the sense of being bound by the fetter of craving in the present.
If other fetters arise with respect to this same object and are present, [the same applies].
Alternatively, when a wholesome mind or an unobscured-neutral mind manifests before one;
or when, in another instance, the fetter of craving manifests before one;
or during a state of non-consciousness—there is no sense of being bound by the manifest fetter of craving.
If there is the present, is there also the past?
Answer: If a prior birth has not been severed, one is bound;
if a prior birth has not yet arisen, or if it has arisen and been severed, one is not bound.
The meaning herein is as explained extensively above.
If, regarding this matter, there is a future fetter of craving (anunaya-saṃyojana), is there also a present one?
Answer: If it is present before one.
The meaning here is also as previously explained.
If there is that which exists in the present, does there also exist that which is in the future?
Answer: It is so.
The meaning herein is as previously explained.

If one is bound by past fetters of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) regarding a certain object, are there also future and present ones? Answer: There are necessarily future ones; as for the present, it depends.
If it is present before one,
the meaning and intent herein are both as previously explained.
If there is that which is future or present, is there also that which is past?
Answer: If that which arose previously has not been severed, one is bound;
if it has not arisen previously, or if having arisen it has been severed, one is not bound.
The meaning here is also as explained before.
If, regarding this object, there is a future fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*), is there also one from the past and the present?
Answer: In this case, there are four permutations (*catuṣkoṭi*).
There may be a future [fetter] without [one from] the past or the present.
This means that regarding this object, the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) has not yet been abandoned;
furthermore, it has not arisen previously, or if it did arise, it has already been abandoned and does not manifest at present.
Herein, the phrase "the fetter of craving has not yet been abandoned" indicates the existence of future craving.
That which has not yet arisen previously, or which, having arisen, has already been abandoned, excludes the existence of past fetters of craving;
that which does not manifest in the present excludes the existence of present fetters of craving.
There may be cases where there is a future and a past [bond of craving] but no present one.
This refers to a case where, regarding a certain object, the bond of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) from a previous life has not been abandoned, yet it does not manifest at present.
Within this context, "the bond of craving from a previous life has not been abandoned" means:
To manifest that there is a past fetter of craving that does not presently manifest is to preclude the existence of a present fetter of craving.
Since the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) from a previous life remains unsevered,
it also implies the existence of the future fetter of craving;
therefore, it is not mentioned separately here.
There may be cases where future and present [fetters] exist, but no past ones;
that is to say, regarding this object, the fetter of craving is present, yet it has not previously arisen, or if it had arisen, it has already been abandoned.
In this context, the statement "the fetter of craving for existence (bhavarāga-saṃyojana) is present" indicates that the fetter of craving for existence exists in the present; however,
the phrase "that which has not yet arisen, or which, having arisen,
has been abandoned" excludes the existence of the fetter of craving for existence in the past.

Since the existence of future [existence] is already indicated by the fact that when the fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) is present, it likewise manifests that future existence, the meaning of future existence is not stated separately.
Alternatively, there may be future [existence] as well as past and present [existence].
This means that regarding this object, there is a fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) that was previously produced and not yet abandoned, and which is also presently manifest.
In this context, the phrase "there is a fetter of craving previously produced and not yet abandoned" indicates the existence of a past fetter of craving.
The phrase "also manifesting before one" indicates the existence of present fetters of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*).
Since past and present fetters of craving exist, it follows by implication that future ones also exist, even if they are not explicitly mentioned.
If there are past and present [fetters], does one also have future [fetters]?
Answer: It is so.
The meaning herein has already been explained as before.
If there is a bond of present craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) regarding this object, is there also [a bond] of the past and future?
Answer: The future is necessarily bound to the past.
If it was not previously severed in a prior birth, then it is bound;
if it had not yet arisen in a prior birth, or if it arose but was subsequently severed, then it is not bound.
The meaning and intent herein are as previously explained.
If there are past and future [phenomena], are there also present ones?
Answer: If they are manifested before one.
The meaning here is also as previously explained.
Just as the fetter of craving (rāga-saṃyojana) passes through six [categories],

it should be understood that the fetters of hostility (pratigha), pride (māna), envy (īrṣyā), and avarice (mātsarya)— as well as the non-universal fetter of ignorance (avidyā-saṃyojana)— pass through the six in the same manner.
Because the meaning of "delusion regarding specific characteristics" (*svalakṣaṇa-saṃyojana*) is similar [to other fetters], they may be categorized as analogous despite differences in their scope.
If there is a past fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) bound to this object, is there also a future one?
Answer: It is so.
If there is the future, is there also the past?
Answer: It is so.
If, regarding this object, there is a bond of past views, is there also one of the present?
Answer: If it is present before one.
If there is a bond of the present, is there also one of the past?
Answer: It is so.
If, with respect to this object, there is a future fetter of views (dṛṣṭisaṃyojana), is there also one that is present?
Answer: If it is manifest.
If there is a present [fetter], is there also a future one? Answer: Yes.
If, regarding this matter, there is a past fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana), is there also a future and a present one?
Answer: It is necessarily bound in the future.
If it is present, it is present before one.
If there is the future and the present, is there also the past?
Answer: It is so. If, regarding this matter, there is bondage by the future fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*), is there also [bondage] by the past and present?
Answer: There is necessarily bondage by the past;
as for the present, it exists if it is currently manifest.
If there is a past [fetter] and a present one, is there also a future one? Answer: Yes.
If, with respect to this object, there is a bond of the present view-fetter (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*), is there also [a bond of] the past and the future?
Answer: It is so.
If there are past and future [dharmas], are there also present ones?
Answer: If they are present before one.

Why is this? It was previously stated that the fetters (*saṃyojana*) which are deluded regarding common characteristics (*sāmānyalakṣaṇa*) are able to act as bonds with respect to the objects belonging to the three realms and five categories.
The past and future [fetters] that have not yet been abandoned bind all things belonging to those three time periods;
the present [fetters] are indeterminate,
meaning they bind only when they are manifest with respect to a particular object.
Because that which is not present before one is not bound.
Just as the fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana) is applied across six [categories],
it should be understood that the same applies to the fetters of grasping (parāmarśa), doubt (vicikitsā), and pervasive ignorance (sarvatraga-avidyā).
Because the meanings of "delusion" (*moha*) and "attachment" (*saṃyojana*) are similar, they may be considered analogous despite differences in their scope.
If there is a bond of past attachment (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) regarding a particular object, is there also a bond of past aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) regarding that same object?
Answer: If that which arose previously has not been abandoned, one is bound;
if it did not arise previously, or if it arose but has already been abandoned, one is not bound.
That is to say, if there is a previously arisen fetter of craving regarding this object that has not been abandoned.
Furthermore, there may be cases where the fetter of hatred (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) produced in a previous life has not yet been abandoned;
in such a case, there is also the sense of being bound by that past fetter of hatred with respect to this very object.

Even if the fetter of attachment (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) produced in a previous life exists with respect to this object and has not been abandoned, yet the fetter of hatred had not previously arisen with respect to it—even if it has arisen elsewhere—it is still said to be "not yet arisen" with respect to this specific object.
If, once it has arisen, it has been abandoned, then with respect to that very object, there is no sense of being bound by the past fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*).
If there is binding by the past fetter of aversion,
is there also binding by the past fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If that which arose previously has not been abandoned, one is bound; if it has not arisen previously, or if having arisen it has been abandoned, one is not bound.
That is to say, if regarding this object there is a previously arisen bond of malice (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) that has not been abandoned.
Furthermore, there may be a case where the fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) from a previous life has not yet been abandoned;
in that case, there is the sense of being bound by the past fetter of craving with respect to that very object.
Even if the fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) from a previous life has not been abandoned with respect to that object, the fetter of craving had not previously arisen toward it.
Even though one has been born elsewhere, with respect to this particular matter it is still said that [the fetter] has not yet arisen;
even if it had arisen and was subsequently severed, there would be no sense of being bound by a past fetter of craving with respect to this matter.
If there is a bond of past craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) regarding this object, is there also a bond of future aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If it has not been abandoned; and how is it that it has not been abandoned?
That is to say, for one who has not yet abandoned the defilement of desire, there is necessarily also the sense of being bound by the future fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*).
If there is the binding of the future fetter of aversion,
does there also exist the binding of the past fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If that which arose previously has not been abandoned, then one is bound;
if it had not arisen previously, or if having arisen it has been abandoned, then one is not bound.
That is to say, if there is a future fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) regarding this object that has not been abandoned.
Furthermore, there may be a case where the fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) belonging to a previous birth has not yet been abandoned;
in that case, there is also the sense of being bound by the past fetter of craving with respect to that very object.

Even if the future fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) toward that object has not yet been abandoned, if the fetter of craving toward it had not previously arisen, [it is not bound by the past fetter].
Even though one has been born elsewhere, with respect to this particular matter, it is still said that [the fetter] has not yet arisen.
Furthermore, if it has already arisen and been abandoned, then regarding this matter, there is no sense of being bound by the past fetter of craving.
If one is bound to this object by the past fetter of craving, is one also bound to it by the present fetter of aversion?
Answer: If it is present.
That is to say, if regarding this object there is a previously arisen fetter of attachment (*rāga-saṃyojana*) that has not yet been abandoned,
and a fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) is also present, then there is the sense of being bound by the presently arisen fetter of aversion.
Or, if regarding this object another fetter arises and becomes present.
Alternatively, when a wholesome mind or an unobscured-neutral mind manifests;
or when, in another instance, the fetter of malice manifests;
or during a state of non-consciousness—there is no sense of being bound by the manifest fetter of malice.
If there is a present fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*), is there also a past fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If it arose previously and has not been abandoned, then one is bound by it;
if it had not arisen previously, or if it arose but has already been abandoned, then one is not bound by it.

This means that if, with respect to a certain object, the fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) is present and the fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) has previously arisen and has not yet been abandoned,
then there is also the sense of being bound by the past fetter of craving with respect to that same object.
If, with respect to this object, although the fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) is present, the fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) has not previously arisen toward it—
even if it arises elsewhere— it is still said that [the fetter of craving] has not arisen with respect to this object.
If, once having arisen, it has been abandoned, then with respect to that object there is no sense of being bound by the fetter of past craving.
If there is binding by the fetter of past craving with respect to an object, is there also binding by the fetter of past or present aversion with respect to that same object?
Answer: In this regard, there are four permutations.
There may be one who is bound by the fetter of past craving, but not bound by the fetters of past or present hatred.
That is to say, regarding this object, there is a previously arisen fetter of craving that has not yet been abandoned;
there is no previously arisen fetter of aversion,
or if one had arisen, it has been abandoned and does not manifest.
In this context, "the fetter of craving for existence (*bhavarāga-saṃyojana*) from a previous birth has not been abandoned" indicates that there is past craving.
"The fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) from a previous birth, even if it arose, has been abandoned" [indicates that there is no present ill-will].
To prevent the existence of past fetters of anger that do not manifest in the present is to prevent the existence of present fetters of anger.
There may be one who is bound by the past fetter of craving and bound by the past fetter of aversion, but not by the present.
This refers to a case where, regarding a certain object, the fetters of craving and aversion arose previously and have not yet been abandoned, while the fetter of aversion is not currently manifest.
In this context, "the fetter of craving and the fetter of aversion that were previously arisen and not yet abandoned" indicates the existence of past fetters of craving and aversion;
"the absence of the fetter of aversion present now" indicates [the absence of] the present fetter of aversion.
There may be the presence of a present fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*),
or there may be the binding of a past fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) as well as the binding of a present fetter of ill-will, but without a past one.
This refers to a case where, regarding this object, there is a previously arisen bond of attachment (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) that has not yet been abandoned;
there is a bond of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) present at the moment, which had not arisen previously, or if it had arisen, it has already been abandoned.
Within this context, "there is a previously arisen bond of attachment that has not yet been abandoned" means:
To say that there is a past fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) while a fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) is present indicates that there is a present fetter of aversion.
As for those [fetters] that have not yet arisen or, having arisen, have already been abandoned,
this excludes the existence of past fetters of malice (*pratigha-saṃyojana*),
or the existence of past fetters of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) that bind one.
Furthermore, there is the case of being bound by past and present fetters of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*).

This refers to when, regarding this very object, the fetter of attachment (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) and the fetter of aversion have arisen previously and have not yet been abandoned, and the fetter of aversion is currently manifest.
In this context, "the fetter of craving and the fetter of aversion that were previously produced and not yet abandoned" indicates the existence of past fetters of craving and aversion;
"the fetter of aversion that is present" [indicates the existence of a current fetter of aversion].
It is evident that there is a present fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*).
If one is bound by a past or present fetter of ill-will,
is one also bound by a past fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If that which arose previously has not been abandoned, one is bound;
if it has not yet arisen, or if it arose but has already been abandoned, one is not bound.
The meaning and intent herein are as explained extensively above.
If, regarding this object, there is bondage by the past fetter of attachment (*anunaya-saṃyojana*), is there also bondage by the future and present fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: In this case, there are three propositions (*trikoṭika*).
There may be one who is bound by the fetter of attachment (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) in the past, but not bound by the fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) in the future or present;
that is to say, regarding phenomena of the form and formless realms, there is a previously arisen fetter of attachment that has not yet been abandoned.
Regarding the phrase "the fetter of craving for existence that was previously produced and not yet abandoned," this indicates the existence of past craving for existence.
As for "dharmas of the form and formless realms":
One may be obstructed from having future and present fetters of malice (*vyāpāda-saṃyojana*), yet lack those fetters of malice; this should be understood as previously explained.
Alternatively, one may be bound by past fetters of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) and bound by future fetters of malice, but not by present ones.

This refers to a case where, regarding this object, there is a previously arisen bond of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) that has not yet been abandoned, as well as a bond of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) that has not yet been abandoned and is not currently manifest.
Regarding the phrase "there is a previously arisen bond of craving that has not yet been abandoned": [it means]...
This indicates that there is a past fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) and that there is a fetter of ill-will (*vyāpāda-saṃyojana*) which has not yet been abandoned;
it indicates that there is a future fetter of ill-will.
Because that which has not been abandoned necessarily possesses the sense of being bound to the future,
the phrase "not present" excludes the existence of a presently active fetter of malice (*pratigha-saṃyojana*).
There may be cases where one is bound by the fetter of attachment (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) in the past and also bound by the fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) in the future and present.
This refers to an object regarding which the fetter of attachment arose previously and has not yet been abandoned, and the fetter of aversion is currently manifest.
In this context, "the fetter of craving for existence that was previously produced and not yet abandoned" indicates the existence of past craving-fetters;
and "the presence of the fetter of aversion" indicates its manifestation in the present.
This demonstrates that there is a present fetter of malice (*pratigha-saṃyojana*).
The existence of this same fetter in the future is established without needing to be stated explicitly,
because whatever exists in the present must necessarily exist in the future.
If there is bondage by the future and present fetters of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*), is there also bondage by the past fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If it was previously produced and not yet abandoned, then there is bondage.
If it has not previously arisen, or if having arisen it has been abandoned, then one is not bound by it;
the meaning of this point is as explained extensively before.
If, regarding this object, there is a bond of past craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*), [one is bound].
Is there also bondage by the fetter of past or future aversion?
The answer is that there are three cases here:
there may be bondage by the fetter of past craving.
There is no past or future fetter of aversion (pratigha-saṃyojana).
This means that regarding the phenomena of the form and formless realms, there is a previously arisen and as-yet-unabandoned fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana).
In this context, the phrase "there is a previously arisen and as-yet-unabandoned fetter of craving" indicates the existence of a past fetter of craving.
Regarding phenomena of the form and formless realms:
it is excluded that there is a past or future fetter of malice (*pratigha-saṃyojana*);
however, there may be a past fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*).
And there is future fetter of ill-will (pratigha-saṃyojana) without past [fetter],
namely: when regarding this object, the previously arisen fetter of craving (rāga-saṃyojana) has not yet been abandoned,
and the fetter of ill-will has also not yet been abandoned.
Furthermore, while the fetter of ill-will (*vyāpāda-saṃyojana*) did not arise previously, or having arisen was already abandoned,
there is here the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) that arose previously and has not yet been abandoned;
this indicates the existence of past craving.
"One who has not yet abandoned the fetter of ill-will" indicates that the future fetter of ill-will exists;
"one who has no fetter of ill-will" means that even if it arose previously, it has been abandoned.
There may be the obstruction of past enmity-ties (*pratigha-saṃyojana*);
or there may be the binding of past affection-ties (*anunaya-saṃyojana*),
as well as the binding of both past and future enmity-ties.
This means that regarding this object, the fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) and the fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) have arisen previously and have not yet been abandoned.
Within this, the phrase "the fetter of craving has arisen previously and has not yet been abandoned" indicates the existence of past craving.
Regarding the statement "there is a previously arisen enmity-fetter (*vyāpāda-saṃyojana*) that has not yet been abandoned":

this indicates that there exists a past enmity-fetter; the existence of its future counterpart is established without needing to be stated explicitly, because wherever there is a past [fetter], there must necessarily be a future one.
If there is a bond of past or future aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*), is there also a bond of past craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If it was previously produced and not yet abandoned, then one is bound.
If it has not yet arisen previously, or if having arisen it has already been abandoned, then one is not bound by it;
the meaning of this point is as explained extensively before.
If, with respect to this object, there is a bond of past craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*), [one is bound].
Is there also bondage by the fetter of ill-will (pratigha-saṃyojana) pertaining to the past, future, and present?
Answer: In this regard, there are five propositions.
There may be bondage by the fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) pertaining to the past.
There is no bondage by the fetter of ill-will (*vyāpāda-saṃyojana*) in the past, future, or present;
that is to say, regarding the phenomena of the form and formless realms, there is a previously arisen craving-fetter (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) that has not yet been abandoned.
Within this context, "previously arisen craving-fetter that has not yet been abandoned" refers to this.

This demonstrates that there is a past fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) regarding phenomena of the form and formless realms, while precluding the existence of a fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) across the three time periods.
Alternatively, there may be the binding of a past fetter of craving as well as the binding of a future fetter of aversion.
There is neither past nor present [bondage],
meaning that regarding this object, there was a craving-fetter (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) in a previous life that has not yet been abandoned,
as well as a hatred-fetter (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) that has not yet been abandoned.
Furthermore, that which has not previously arisen, or having arisen has been severed and does not manifest before one—
among these, the statement "there is a fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) that was previously unsevered" indicates the existence of a past fetter of craving.
The phrase "there is one for whom the fetter of ill-will has not been abandoned" indicates that the future fetter of ill-will exists;
whereas that which has not yet arisen, or which, having arisen, has already been abandoned, does not.
The absence of the past fetter of ill-will (pratigha-saṃyojana) means that it does not manifest in the present; or,
there may be the bondage of the past fetter of craving (anunaya-saṃyojana).
Furthermore, there is the case where one is bound by future and present fetters of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*),
but not by past ones; that is to say, regarding this very object, the fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) has arisen previously and has not yet been abandoned,
and the fetter of aversion is currently manifest.
Furthermore, that which has not yet arisen previously, or which, having arisen, has already been abandoned—
this refers to the presence of the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) from a prior life that was not yet abandoned,
thereby demonstrating that there is a past fetter of craving and a present fetter of malice (*pratigha-saṃyojana*).
This demonstrates that there is the present fetter of ill-will (*vyāpāda-saṃyojana*).
That this exists in the future is established even without being explicitly stated;
the meaning is as previously explained.
Regarding those that have not previously arisen, or having arisen have been abandoned:
this excludes the existence of past fetters of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*).
Alternatively, there may be past fetters of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) and past and future fetters of aversion, but none that are present.

This refers to a case where, regarding a certain object, the fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) and the fetter of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) arose previously and have not yet been abandoned, yet the fetter of aversion is not currently manifest.
Regarding this, "the fetter of craving arose previously and has not yet been abandoned" means:
The statement "there is a past fetter of craving" indicates that there is a past fetter of craving;
the statement "there is a previously arisen fetter of aversion that has not been abandoned" indicates that there is a past fetter of aversion.
The existence of these future [fetters] is established even without being explicitly stated;
the meaning is as previously explained.
As for the absence of the fetter of malice (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) manifesting in the present:
There may be one who possesses the present fetter of malice (*pratigha-saṃyojana*),
or who is bound by the past fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*),
as well as being bound by the past, future, and present fetters of malice.

This means that regarding this object, there is a previously arisen and as-yet-unabandoned bond of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) and a bond of aversion (*pratigha-saṃyojana*) that is currently manifest.
Among these, "there is a previously arisen and as-yet-unabandoned bond of craving" refers to the following:
The statement "there is a past fetter of craving" indicates that there is a past fetter of craving;
the statement "there is a previously arisen fetter of hostility that has not yet been abandoned" indicates that there is a past fetter of hostility.
"When the fetter of ill-will (vyāpāda-saṃyojana) is present" indicates that the fetter of ill-will exists in the present;
its existence in the future is not explicitly stated, yet it is established by implication.
Since that which exists in the past and present must also exist in the future,
if one is bound by the fetter of malice (*vyāpāda-saṃyojana*) in the past, future, and present,
is one also bound by the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) in the past?
Answer: If that which arose previously has not been severed, one is bound;
if it had not arisen previously, or if having arisen it has been severed, one is not bound.
The meaning and intent herein are as explained extensively before.
As it is with the fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*), so it is with the fetters of envy (*īrṣyā*) and avarice (*mātsarya*);
this is because they all belong exclusively to the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*).
Therefore, by contrasting craving (*tṛṣṇā*) with them, one forms the "small sevenfold set" (*sapta-laghu-vākya*).
Regarding the distinctions as explained for the fetter of ill-will (*pratigha-saṃyojana*):
with respect to the factors of the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*) to be abandoned by insight (*darśana-prahātavya*).
Regarding the dharmas of the form and formless realms:
there is the fetter of craving (anunaya-saṃyojana) that arose previously and has not yet been abandoned;
however, there is no past, future, or present fetter of envy (īrṣyā-saṃyojana) or stinginess (mātsarya-saṃyojana).
In this context, the phrase "the fetter of craving for intermediate existence (*antarābhava*) that was previously produced and not yet abandoned" clarifies two of the seven propositions.
This refers to the past fetter of craving for intermediate existence directed toward phenomena in the desire realm to be abandoned by insight (*darśana-heya*),
as well as toward phenomena in the form and formless realms, wherein there are no fetters of envy (*īrṣyā*) or avarice (*mātsarya*) across the three time periods.
This excludes the two sets of seven phrases.
Among these, there are past, future, and present fetters of envy (*īrṣyā*) and avarice (*mātsarya*).
These differ from the preceding [fetters] in that they pertain to phenomena (*dharma*) in the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*) that are to be abandoned by insight (*darśana-prahātavya*).
Since the two fetters of envy (*īrṣyā*) and avarice (*mātsarya*) are abandoned only through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*),
if there is a past bond of the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) regarding a certain object, is there also a past bond of the fetter of pride (*māna-saṃyojana*) regarding that same object?
Answer: If that which arose previously has not been severed, then one is bound;
if it has not yet arisen, or if it arose but has already been severed, then one is not bound.

That is to say, regarding this object, if there is a previously arisen fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) that has not been severed, and there is also a previously arisen fetter of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*) that has not been severed.
In this very case, there is also the sense of being bound by the fetter of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*) in the past.
Even if, regarding this object, the previously arisen fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) has not yet been abandoned, the fetter of conceit had not previously arisen with respect to it.
Although one may have been born elsewhere, with respect to this particular matter, it is still said that [the fetter] has not yet arisen.
Even if it had arisen and was subsequently abandoned, there would be no sense of being bound by the past fetter of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*) regarding this very matter.
If there is a past fetter of conceit (māna-saṃyojana), is there also a past fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana)?
Answer: If it was produced in a previous life and has not yet been abandoned, then one is bound by it.
If [the fetter] has not previously arisen, or if it has arisen but been abandoned, then one is not bound by it. That is to say,
regarding this particular object, if there is a previously arisen fetter of conceit that has not been abandoned,
and there is also a previously arisen fetter of craving that has not been abandoned.
In this very case, there is also the sense of being bound by the fetter of past craving.
Even if the fetter of conceit from a previous life has not yet been abandoned regarding this object, the fetter of craving had not previously arisen in relation to it.
Even though one has been born elsewhere, with respect to this particular matter it is still said that [the fetter] has not yet arisen.
Furthermore, if it has already arisen and been abandoned, then with respect to this very matter, there is no sense of being bound by the past fetter of craving.
If there is bondage by the past fetter of craving regarding this object, is there also bondage by the future fetter of conceit?
Answer: It is so.
Why is this? It is because it was previously stated that the fetter of pride (*māna-saṃyojana*) is able to act as a bond for the five categories of phenomena within the three realms;
since it has not yet been abandoned in the future, it will certainly bind all phenomena of the three times.
If there is a future fetter of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*) that binds, is there also a past fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) that binds?
Answer: If it arose previously and has not been abandoned, then one is bound;
if it did not arise previously, or if it arose and has already been abandoned, then one is not bound.
That is to say, if regarding this object there is a future fetter of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*) that has not yet been abandoned,
and there is also a previously arisen fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) that has not yet been abandoned,
then regarding that same object there is also the sense of being bound by a past fetter of craving.
If, regarding this particular object, although the future fetter of conceit (*māna*) has not yet been abandoned, the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā*) had not previously arisen toward it;
even though it may have arisen elsewhere, with respect to this specific object, it is said that [the fetter] has not yet arisen.
If, once it has arisen, it is already abandoned, then there is no sense in which one is bound to that object by the past fetter of craving.
If one is bound to an object by the past fetter of craving,
is one also bound to that same object by the present fetter of conceit?
Answer: If it is present before one— that is,
if regarding this object there is a previously arisen fetter of craving that has not yet been abandoned,
and the fetter of conceit is also present before one— then there is the sense of being bound by the present fetter of conceit.
If, with respect to this object, other fetters (*saṃyojana*) arise and become manifest;
or if wholesome or non-obscured-neutral minds arise and become manifest;
or if the fetter of pride (*māna*) arises and becomes manifest with respect to another object.
Or, at a time when one is without mind, there is no sense of being bound by the present fetter of conceit (*māna*).
Even if there were binding by the present fetter of conceit,
would there also be binding by the past fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā*)?
Answer: If it has arisen previously and has not been abandoned, one is bound;
if it has not arisen previously, or if it arose but has already been abandoned, one is not bound.
That is to say, if the fetter of conceit (māna-saṃyojana) is present with respect to this object.

Furthermore, there is also the sense that even when the fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) from a previous life has not yet been abandoned, one is bound by that past fetter of craving with respect to this very object.
Even if the fetter of pride (*māna-saṃyojana*) is present with respect to this object, it may be that the fetter of craving had not previously arisen toward it.
Even if one has been born elsewhere, with respect to this matter it is still called "not yet arisen.
Furthermore, if [the fetter] has already arisen and been abandoned, then regarding this matter, there is no sense of being bound by the past fetter of craving.
If there is a bond of past craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) regarding this object, is there also a bond of past and present conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: In this case, there are four permutations (*catuṣkoṭi*).
There may be one who is bound by the fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) in the past, but not bound by the fetter of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*) in the past or present.
This refers to a case where, regarding this object, the fetter of craving arose previously and has not yet been abandoned,
whereas the fetter of conceit did not arise previously, or having arisen, has already been abandoned and does not manifest at present.
In this context, "the fetter of craving for existence (bhavarāga-saṃyojana) from a previous life has not been abandoned" indicates that the past fetter of craving for existence remains unsevered;
"the fetter of pride (māna-saṃyojana) from a previous life, even if it arose, has been severed" indicates that it has been abandoned.
The obstruction of past pride-fetters (māna-saṃyojana) means that they do not manifest in the present;
the obstruction of present pride-fetters means that there may be bonds of past craving-fetters (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana).
Furthermore, there is the case where one is bound by the past fetter of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*) but not by the present one;
that is to say, regarding this object, the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) and the fetter of conceit have arisen previously and have not yet been abandoned,
yet the fetter of conceit is not currently manifest.
Regarding the phrase "those who have not previously abandoned the fetter of craving and the fetter of pride":
this indicates that they possess past fetters of craving and pride;
"without the fetter of pride present now" means that the fetter of pride does not currently manifest.
There are cases where there is the present fetter of pride,
or where there is the past fetter of craving and the present fetter of pride, but no past [fetter].
This refers to a case where, regarding this object, there is a previously arisen fetter of craving that has not yet been abandoned,
and there is a fetter of pride present before one, which had not previously arisen or, if it had arisen, has already been abandoned. Among these,
"there is a previously arisen fetter of craving that has not yet been abandoned" means:
To manifest that there is a past fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) means to manifest that there is a present fetter of pride (*māna-saṃyojana*).
Regarding those [fetters] that have not yet arisen in the past, or those that have arisen but have already been abandoned:
this excludes the existence of past fetters of conceit (*māna*),
or the existence of past fetters of craving (*anunaya*) that bind one.

Furthermore, there is the bondage of the past and present fetter of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*) regarding this object, meaning that the fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) and the fetter of conceit have arisen previously and have not yet been abandoned, and the fetter of conceit is currently manifest.
In this context, "the fetter of craving and the fetter of pride that were previously produced and not yet abandoned" indicates the existence of past fetters of craving and pride;
"the fetter of pride that is present" indicates the existence of a present fetter of pride.
If there is a past or present fetter of conceit (māna-saṃyojana), is there also a past fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana)?
Answer: If it was not abandoned in a previous birth, then one is bound by it.
If it has not previously arisen, or if having arisen it has been abandoned, then one is not bound by it;
the meaning and intent of this point are as explained extensively before.
If one is bound to this object by the past fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*), is one also bound to it by the future and present fetters of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: That which is necessarily bound in the future is necessarily bound in the present if it manifests before one.

Herein, "necessarily bound in the future" means that as long as the fetter of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*) of the future has not been abandoned, it is definitively bound to all objects belonging to the five categories across the three realms.
Regarding "present" or "manifesting in the present," the meaning is as previously explained.
Suppose there is a bond of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*) belonging to the future or the present;
would there also be a bond of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) belonging to the past?
Answer: If that which arose previously has not been severed, one is bound;
if it has not arisen previously, or if it has arisen but has already been severed, one is not bound.
The meaning and intent herein are as explained extensively above.
If there is bondage by the past fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) regarding this object, is there also bondage by the past and future fetter of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: Regarding the future, there is necessarily bondage; regarding the past, it depends.
If that which arose previously has not been severed, one is bound;
if it has not yet arisen, or if it arose but has already been severed, one is not bound.
Regarding these two points, both are as explained previously.
If there is a bond of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*) belonging to the past or the future, is there also a bond of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) belonging to the past?
Answer: If it was previously produced and has not yet been abandoned, then one is bound.
If it has not yet arisen previously, or if having arisen it has been severed, then one is not bound by it;
the meaning here is also as explained before.
If there is a past fetter of craving (anunaya-saṃyojana) bound to this object, [then one is bound].
Is there also the bondage of the fetter of pride (māna-saṃyojana) belonging to the past, future, and present?
Answer: There are four permutations (catuṣkoṭika) in this regard.
There may be the bondage of the fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) belonging to the past and the bondage of the fetter of pride belonging to the future.
There is no past or present [defilement].
This means that regarding this object, the fetter of craving (rāga-saṃyojana) from a previous life has not been abandoned;
however, the fetter of pride (māna-saṃyojana) from a previous life, even if it had arisen, has already been abandoned and does not manifest at present.
In this context, the statement that "the fetter of craving (rāga-saṃyojana) from previous lives has not been severed" indicates the existence of past craving;
whereas the statement that "the fetter of pride (māna-saṃyojana) from previous lives has been severed even if it arose" excludes the existence of past pride.
"Not being present" excludes the existence of the present fetter of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*);
the existence of this [fetter] in the future is established by implication without needing to be stated.
Because that fetter of craving has not yet been abandoned, this conceit must necessarily exist.
Alternatively, there may be the past fetter of craving,
as well as the past and future fetters of conceit, but none in the present.

This means that regarding this object, there are the fetters of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) and pride (*māna-saṃyojana*) produced in a prior life that have not yet been abandoned, and the fetter of pride manifests in the present.
Regarding the phrase "there are the fetters of craving and pride produced in a prior life that have not yet been abandoned": [it refers to these two being present].
To state that there are past fetters of craving and pride,
but no pride-fetter is present,
is to preclude the existence of a present pride-fetter.
This future existence is established as a matter of course even without being explicitly stated;
its meaning is as previously explained.
Alternatively, there may be one who is bound by the fetter of craving belonging to the past.
Furthermore, there are cases where one is bound by the fetter of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*) in the future and present,
but not in the past; that is to say, regarding this same object, the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) existed in a prior life and was not yet abandoned,
and the fetter of conceit is manifest in the present, whereas it did not exist in a prior life, or having arisen, had already been abandoned.
In this context, "the fetter of craving for existence (*bhavarāga-saṃyojana*) that was previously produced and not yet abandoned" indicates the existence of past craving;
"the fetter of pride (*māna-saṃyojana*) that is present" [indicates its current state].
This demonstrates that there is the fetter of pride in the present,
while the absence of it in previous lives— even if it had arisen there—
indicates that the fetter of pride in the past does not exist.
This future existence is established by implication without needing to be stated explicitly,
because whenever the fetter of conceit (*māna*) manifests in the present, it necessarily entails its presence in the future.
Alternatively, there may be a connection with the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā*) belonging to the past.
There is also bondage by the fetter of conceit (*māna-saṃyojana*) belonging to the past, future, and present.
That is to say, regarding this object, there is the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) and the fetter of conceit that arose previously and have not yet been abandoned,
as well as the fetter of conceit that is currently manifest.
In this context, the phrase "those who have not yet abandoned the fetter of craving and the fetter of conceit born in previous lives" indicates the existence of past fetters of craving and conceit;
the phrase "those for whom the fetter of conceit is present" indicates its current manifestation.
This demonstrates that there is the fetter of pride (*māna-saṃyojana*) in the present;
its existence in the future is established without needing to be stated,
as the meaning has been explained previously.
If there is a bond of the conceit-fetters (*māna-saṃyojana*) belonging to the past, future, or present, is there also a bond of the craving-fetters (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) belonging to the past?
Answer: If it was previously produced and not yet abandoned, then one is bound.
If it has not yet arisen previously, or if having arisen it has already been abandoned, then one is not bound by it;
the meaning of this point is as explained extensively before.
If, with respect to this object, there is a past fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*), [one is bound].
Is there also the fetter of past ignorance?
Answer: It is so. Why is that?

It was previously stated that the various fetters (saṃyojana) which delude one regarding common characteristics (sāmānya-lakṣaṇa) can act as bonds for objects belonging to the five categories (pañca-prakāra) across the three realms (traidhātuka).
If these have not been abandoned in the past, they certainly bind all such objects throughout the three periods of time.
Since ignorance is also a fetter of common characteristics, the answer is "yes.
If there is a past fetter of ignorance that binds one, is there also a past fetter of craving that binds one?
Answer: If it has arisen previously and has not been abandoned, one is bound by it;
if it has not arisen previously, or if it arose but has already been abandoned, one is not bound by it.
That is to say, regarding this object, if there is a previously arisen fetter of ignorance that has not been abandoned.
Furthermore, there may be a case where the fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) from a previous birth has not yet been abandoned;
in that case, there is also the sense of being bound by the past fetter of craving with respect to that very object.
Even if the fetter of ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*) from a previous birth has not been abandoned with respect to that object, [the same principle applies].
Furthermore, regarding this [object], although the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) had not previously arisen,
even if it were to arise elsewhere, it is still said with respect to this specific object that it has "not yet arisen.
Even if it had arisen and was subsequently abandoned, there is no sense of being bound by a past fetter of craving with respect to this very object.
If, regarding this matter, there is bondage by the past fetter of craving, is there also bondage by the future fetter of ignorance?
Answer: It is so. Why is that?
It was stated previously that the fetters (*saṃyojana*) of common characteristics (*sāmānyalakṣaṇa*) can act as bonds for the objects of the five categories (*pañcavastuka*) across the three realms;
this is because those [fetters] of the future, when not yet abandoned, definitely bind all objects of the three times.
If there is a bond of future ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*), is there also a bond of past craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If it was not severed in a previous birth, then one is bound.
If [the fetter] has not previously arisen, or if having arisen it has already been abandoned, then one is not bound by it.
That is to say, regarding this object, if there is a future fetter of ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*) that has not yet been abandoned,
and there is also a previously arisen fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) that has not yet been abandoned.
In this very case, there is also the sense of being bound by the fetter of past craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*).
Even if, regarding this object, the fetter of future ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*) has not yet been abandoned, the fetter of craving had not previously arisen with respect to it.
Even though one has been born in another place, with respect to this matter it is still said that [the fetter] has not yet arisen.
Even if it had arisen and was subsequently abandoned, there would be no sense of being bound by the past fetter of craving with respect to this matter.
If, regarding this matter, there is bondage by the past fetter of craving (anunaya-saṃyojana), is there also bondage by the present fetter of ignorance (avidyā-saṃyojana)?
Answer: If it is present.
That is to say, if regarding this object there is a previously arisen fetter of craving that has not yet been abandoned,
and the fetter of ignorance is also present, then there is the sense of being bound by the presently occurring fetter of ignorance.
If, with respect to this object, either a wholesome or an unobscured-neutral mind manifests,
or if elsewhere the fetter of ignorance manifests, or during a state of non-consciousness, then there is no sense of being bound by the present fetter of ignorance.
If there is a bond of the fetter of ignorance (avidyā-saṃyojana) in the present, is there also a bond of the fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) in the past?
Answer: If it was not abandoned in a previous life, then one is bound.
If [the fetter] has not previously arisen, or if having arisen it has already been abandoned, then one is not bound by it.
That is to say, regarding a given object, if the fetter of ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*) is present,
and there is also the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) that arose previously and has not yet been abandoned.
In this very case, there is also the sense of being bound by the fetter of past craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*).
Even if the fetter of ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*) is present with respect to this object,
the fetter of craving had not previously arisen therein.
Even if one has been born elsewhere, with respect to this matter it is still said that [the fetter] has not yet arisen.
Even if it had arisen and was subsequently abandoned, there would be no sense of being bound by a past fetter of craving with respect to this matter;
for if there were such a binding by a past fetter of craving with respect to this matter, [it would be impossible].
Is there also bondage by the fetter of ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*) belonging to the past and the present?
Answer: One is necessarily bound by that of the past; as for the present, one is bound if it is currently manifest.
The meaning and intent herein are the same as previously explained.
If there is a bond of past and present ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*), is there also a bond of past craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If it was not abandoned in a previous life, then one is bound.
If it has not yet arisen previously, or if having arisen it has already been abandoned, then one is not bound by it;
the meaning of this point is as explained extensively before.
If there is a bond of past craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) regarding this object, [one is bound].
Is there also bondage by the fetter of ignorance regarding the future and the present?
Answer: One is necessarily bound to the future; as for the present, one is bound if it is manifest before one.
The meaning and intent here are both as previously explained.
If there is bondage by the fetter of ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*) in the future and present, is there also bondage by the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) in the past?
Answer: If it was not severed in a previous life, then one is bound.
If [a defilement] has not previously arisen, or if it has arisen but has already been abandoned, then one is not bound by it;
the meaning of this point is as explained at length previously.
Regarding this matter:
If there is bondage by the past fetter of craving, is there also bondage by the past and future fetters of ignorance?
Answer: It is so.
Why is this? It is because it was previously stated that the fetters of common characteristics (*sāmānyalakṣaṇa*) can act as bonds for the objects of the five categories within the three realms;
since those [fetters] of the past and future, when not yet abandoned, definitely bind all objects across the three times.
If there is a bond of past and future ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*), is there also a bond of past craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: If it was not severed in a previous life, then one is bound.
If it has not previously arisen, or if having arisen it has been abandoned, then one is not bound by it;
the meaning of this point is explained in detail as previously stated.
If, with respect to this object, there is a bond of past craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*), [one is bound].
Is there also bondage by the fetter of ignorance (*avidyā-saṃyojana*) regarding the past, future, and present?
Answer: One is necessarily bound by the past and the future;
as for the present, one is bound if it is currently manifest.
The meaning here is entirely as previously explained.
Suppose there is a bond of ignorance (avidyā-saṃyojana) belonging to the past, future, or present;
would there also be a bond of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) belonging to the past?
Answer: If that which arose previously has not been severed, then one is bound;
if it has not arisen previously, or if it arose but has already been severed, then one is not bound.
The meaning and intent herein are as explained extensively before.

translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang under imperial decree. Section Two: The Aggregate of Fetters (Saṃyojana-skandha), Sub-section Two: The Chapter on Singlefold [Factors], Part Four. If, with respect to this object, there is the bondage of the past fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*).
Is there also bondage by the past fetter of views?
Answer: If it has not been abandoned;
that is to say, if regarding this object there exists a previously arisen fetter of craving that has not yet been abandoned.
The fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) has also not yet been abandoned;
thus, with respect to this very object, there is also the sense of being bound by the past fetter of views.
Even if, with respect to this object, the previously arisen fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) remains unabandoned, the fetter of views has already been abandoned.
In this case, there is no sense of being bound by the fetter of views regarding the past,
just as when the subsequent knowledge of the path (*mārgānvayajñāna*) has already arisen,
there may still be a previously arisen and unsevered fetter of craving toward phenomena to be abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).

When the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudayānvaya-jñāna*) has already arisen, there exist factors dissociated from the fetters of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) that are to be abandoned by the vision of cessation and the path;
furthermore, the previously arisen fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) has not yet been abandoned.
It is for this reason [that the condition is established].
In this context, the general statement "if not yet abandoned" does not refer to the stage prior to the arising of the subsequent knowledge of the path (mārga-anvaya-jñāna),
because at that stage there is still craving for existence (bhavarāga) and the absence of views (dṛṣṭi).
Because the past fetter of delusion regarding common characteristics (*sāmānyalakṣaṇa*), if not yet abandoned, necessarily binds to objects belonging to all three time periods;
it is not like craving (*tṛṣṇā*) and other fetters for which an indeterminate statement is made.
Even if there were a past fetter of views (*dṛṣṭisaṃyojana*), [it would likewise bind to all three times].
Furthermore, is there also bondage by the fetter of craving belonging to the past?
Answer: If it arose previously and has not been abandoned, then there is bondage;
if it did not arise previously, or if it arose but has already been abandoned, then there is no bondage.
That is to say, if regarding this object there is a previously arisen fetter of views (*dṛṣṭisaṃyojana*) that has not yet been abandoned,
and there is also a previously arisen fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇāsaṃyojana*) that has not yet been abandoned,
then regarding that very object there is the sense of being bound by a past fetter of craving.
If, regarding this particular object, although the previously arisen fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana) has not yet been abandoned,
the previously unarisen fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) has not arisen with respect to it—
even if it has arisen elsewhere— it is still said to be "unarisen" with respect to this object.
If [the fetter] has already been abandoned once it has arisen,
then there is no sense of being bound by the past fetter of craving regarding that object.
If one were bound by the past fetter of craving regarding that object, [it would not have been abandoned].
Is there also future fettering by the fetter of views?
Answer: If it has not been abandoned;
that is to say, if regarding this object, the previously arisen fetter of craving has not been abandoned and the fetter of views has also not been abandoned.
In this very case, there is also the sense of being bound by the future fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*). Even if,
regarding this object, the previously arisen fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) has not yet been abandoned,
the fetter of views has already been abandoned.
In that case, there is no sense of being bound by the fetter of views regarding the future.
The rest is as previously explained.
Furthermore, if one is bound by the fetter of views regarding the future, is one also bound by the fetter of craving regarding the past?
Answer: If it has previously arisen and has not been abandoned, one is bound to it;
if it has not previously arisen, or if it arose but has already been abandoned, one is not bound to it—referring to this particular object.
If there is a future fetter of views that has not yet been abandoned,
and there is also a previously arisen fetter of craving that has not yet been abandoned,
then with respect to that very object, there is also the sense of being bound by a past fetter of craving.
If, with respect to this object, although the future fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) has not yet been abandoned,
the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) had not previously arisen toward it—
even if it arises elsewhere— it is nonetheless said that [the fetter of craving] has not arisen with respect to this object.
If [the past fetter] has already been abandoned upon arising,
then there is no sense of being bound by the past fetter of craving with respect to that object. If there is binding by the past fetter of craving with respect to an object,
is there also binding by the present fetter of views with respect to that same object?
Answer: If it is present before one—
meaning that regarding this object, if there is a previously arisen fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) that has not yet been abandoned,
and the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) is also present before one— then there is the sense of being bound by the present fetter of views.
If, regarding this object,
other fetters arise and become manifest,
or a wholesome or non-obscured neutral mind arises and becomes manifest.
Alternatively, the fetter of views may arise and become manifest in another location;
or, during a state of mindlessness, there is no sense of being bound by the fetter of views in the present.
Even if there were such a case of being bound by the fetter of views in the present, [it would not apply here].
Furthermore, is there also bondage by the fetter of craving for the past?
Answer: If it arose previously and has not been abandoned, then one is bound;
if it had not arisen previously, or if it arose but has already been abandoned, then one is not bound.
That is to say, if, with respect to this object, the fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana) is present,
and the previously arisen fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) has not yet been abandoned,
then there is also the sense of being bound by the past fetter of craving with respect to that same object.
If, regarding this particular object, although the fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana) is present,
yet the fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) has not previously arisen with respect to it—
even if it arises elsewhere— it is still said that [the fetter] has not arisen with respect to this object.
If [the fetter] has already been abandoned once it has arisen,
then with respect to that object, there is no sense of being bound by the past fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*).
If, with respect to an object, there is binding by the past fetter of craving, is there also binding by the past and present fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*)?
Answer: There are three propositions here.
First, there may be one who is bound by the fetter of craving (rāga-saṃyojana) in the past, but is not bound by the fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana) in the past or present.

This means that regarding this object, the fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) produced in a prior life has not yet been abandoned, while the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) has already been abandoned.
In this context, the phrase "the fetter of craving produced in a prior life has not yet been abandoned" indicates the existence of past craving.
Regarding one for whom the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) has already been abandoned, this excludes the existence of past or present fetters of views;
that is to say, when the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaya-anvaya-jñāna*) has arisen,
there is no longer association with those factors to be abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-heya*) or the path (*mārga-darśana-heya*) that constitute the fetter of views.
There is the case where the fetter of craving for previous births has not yet been abandoned,
and the knowledge of the path-type (mārga-anvaya-jñāna) has already arisen,
with respect to phenomena to be abandoned through cultivation (bhāvanā-heya-dharma).
There is one for whom the fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) of a previous birth has not yet been abandoned;
or there is one who is bound by the fetter of craving of the past and bound by the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) of the past,
but not by those of the present.
This refers to a case where, regarding this object, there is a previously arisen fetter of craving that has not yet been abandoned,
as well as a fetter of views that has not yet been abandoned but is not currently manifest.
Regarding this, "there is a previously arisen fetter of craving that has not yet been abandoned" means:
The existence of past fetters of craving is indicated;
the fact that the fetters of views have not yet been abandoned indicates the existence of past fetters of views.
Because for one who has not yet abandoned [the defilements], there must necessarily be a past fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana) regarding the objects to which they are bound;
the phrase "but it does not manifest" serves to exclude the possibility of a present fetter of views.
There may be one who is bound by the fetter of craving (*anunaya-saṃyojana*) belonging to the past,
and also bound by the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) belonging to both the past and the present;
that is to say, regarding this particular object, there was a previously arisen fetter of craving that has not yet been abandoned.
There is also the case where the fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana) is present;
herein, the phrase "the fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) that arose previously has not been abandoned" indicates the existence of past craving.
"Furthermore, there is also the presence of the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) in the present" indicates that the fetter of views exists in the present;
the fact that it existed in the past is established by implication and need not be stated explicitly.
Since the past view-fetters (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana) must necessarily exist when the present view-fetters manifest,
if there is bondage by the past and present view-fetters,
is there also bondage by the past craving-fetters (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana)?
Answer: If that which arose previously has not been abandoned, one is bound;
if it has not yet arisen, or if it arose but has already been abandoned, one is not bound.
The meaning and intent herein are as explained extensively above.
If there is bondage by the past fetter of craving (anunaya-saṃyojana) regarding this object, is there also bondage by the future and present fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana)?
Answer: In this case, there are three propositions.
There may be one who is bound by the fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) in the past,
but not bound by the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) in the future or present;
that is to say, regarding this object, the fetter of craving arose previously and has not yet been abandoned.
When it is seen that the fetter of views has already been severed,
the statement that "the fetter of craving for existence (bhavarāga) which existed previously in this [life] has not yet been severed" indicates the existence of past craving-fetters.
Regarding one for whom the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭisaṃyojana*) has already been abandoned:
this precludes the existence of future or present fetters of views.
The remainder is as previously explained.
There may be one who is bound by the fetter of craving (*rāga-saṃyojana*) in the past and bound by the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*) in the future, but not in the present.
This refers to a case where, regarding a particular object, the fetter of craving arose previously and has not yet been abandoned.
Furthermore, there are cases where the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭisaṃyojana*) has not been abandoned but is not currently manifest.

Among these, the phrase "the fetter of craving for existence (*bhavarāgasaṃyojana*) that arose in a previous life and has not been abandoned" indicates that there exists a past fetter of craving for existence and a fetter of views that have not yet been abandoned.
This demonstrates that there exists a future fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*).
This is because, as long as it has not been abandoned, there must necessarily be a binding by the future fetter of views regarding the objects to which one is bound;
yet, it does not manifest in the present.
There is the case where there is no present fetter of views (*dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana*),
yet there is a past fetter of craving (*tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana*) as well as a future and present fetter of views.
This refers to an object regarding which a previously arisen fetter of craving has not yet been abandoned.
Furthermore, when the fetter of views (*dṛṣṭisaṃyojana*) is present,
if there is a fetter of craving for existence (*bhavarāgasaṃyojana*) that was previously produced and not yet abandoned,
this indicates the existence of a past fetter of craving.
"When there is a manifest fetter of views" indicates that the fetter of views exists in the present;
its existence in the future is established as a matter of course and need not be explicitly stated.
Because when the fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana) is present, it necessarily exists in the future as well.
If one is bound by the fetter of views in the future and present,
is one also bound by the fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) in the past?
Answer: If that which arose previously has not been severed, then one is bound;
if it had not arisen previously, or if it arose but has since been severed, then one is not bound.
The meaning and intent herein are as explained extensively above.
If, regarding this object, there is bondage by the past fetter of craving (rāga-saṃyojana), is there also bondage by the past and future fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana)?
Answer: If it has not been abandoned.
The meaning herein should be understood as previously explained.
Suppose there is bondage by the fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana) pertaining to the past and future;
would there also be bondage by the fetter of craving (tṛṣṇā-saṃyojana) pertaining to the past?
Answer: If that which arose previously has not been severed, one is bound;
if it has not yet arisen, or if having arisen it has already been severed, one is not bound.
The meaning and intent herein are as explained extensively before.
If, regarding this object, there is bondage by the past fetter of craving (rāga-saṃyojana), is there also bondage by the past, future, and present fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana)?
Answer: In this case, there are three propositions (trikoṭika).
There may be one who is bound by the fetter of craving (anunaya-saṃyojana) in the past,
but not bound by the fetter of views (dṛṣṭi-saṃyojana) in the past, future, or present;
that is to say, regarding this object, the previously arisen fetter of craving has not yet been abandoned.
Regarding the statement "the fetter of views has already been abandoned":
this indicates that there are cases where the fetter of craving for existence (*bhavarāga*) was previously un-abandoned,
such that while the fetter of craving for existence exists in the past, the fetter of views has already been abandoned.
It excludes the fetters of views pertaining to the past, future, and present;

that is to say, it refers to those factors dissociated from the fetters of views to be abandoned through the vision of cessation and the path, once the subsequent knowledge of origin (*samudaye anvaya-jñāna*) has already arisen.
There is the fetter of craving that arose previously and has not yet been abandoned;
